definition_zh: 研究设计；研究方案；研究架构
definition_en: the overall plan that specifies how a study will collect, measure and analyse evidence in order to answer a research question
core_image: 桌上摊开一张流程图，顶端写着研究问题，往下分出抽样、测量、时点与统计四列，角落贴满修订便签
scene: 开题会上，导师把一张流程图铺在桌面，问题写在顶端，往下分出抽样、工具、时点与统计四列，桌角还压着一叠修改稿。A sound research design states whom to study, what to measure and when to stop.
sceneCN: 这里指一项研究的总体方案（第 1 个义项：研究的总体计划）；句意为严谨的研究设计会说明研究谁、测量什么以及何时停止。图中可辨识物件：流程图、研究问题卡片、抽样框、测量工具、时间轴、统计表。

pos.zh: 研究设计；研究方案；研究架构

derivatives.zh: 由古法语 recerche 而来，义为「研究；调查」
由研究动词加表示施动者的词尾构成，义为「研究者」
由拉丁语 designare 经法语而来，义为「设计；方案」
由设计动词加表示施动者的词尾构成，义为「设计者」
由表示「重新」的前缀加设计动词构成，义为「重新设计」

senses.title: The overall plan of a study
senses.definition: the complete plan that states the question, the evidence needed and the steps for gathering it
senses.definitionCN: 说明研究问题、所需证据与收集步骤的完整计划
senses.example: The research design must be approved before any data are collected.
senses.exampleCN: 在任何数据收集之前，研究设计必须先获批准。
senses.why: A study is built twice, once on paper and once in the field, and this sense names the paper version.
senses.whyCN: 研究要建两次，一次在纸上，一次在现场，这个义项指纸上的那一版。

senses.title: The choice of a research strategy
senses.definition: the decision to use quantitative, qualitative or mixed methods and the reasons given for that choice
senses.definitionCN: 决定采用定量、定性或混合方法，并说明这样选择的理由
senses.example: Their research design combines interviews with a large survey.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的研究设计把访谈与大规模问卷结合起来。
senses.why: Before any instrument is chosen, the study must decide what kind of evidence will count as an answer.
senses.whyCN: 在选定任何工具之前，研究必须先决定什么样的证据才算答案。

senses.title: The arrangement of comparison and control
senses.definition: the way participants are assigned to groups and the way rival explanations are ruled out
senses.definitionCN: 安排参与者如何分组，以及如何排除其他可能的解释
senses.example: An experimental research design assigns participants to groups at random.
senses.exampleCN: 实验性研究设计把参与者随机分配到各组。
senses.why: A claim about cause needs a contrast, and the plan must build that contrast before the first measurement.
senses.whyCN: 关于因果的主张需要一个对照，而方案必须在第一次测量之前把这个对照搭好。

senses.title: The plan for selecting participants
senses.definition: the specification of the population, the sampling frame and the rules for including or excluding cases
senses.definitionCN: 明确总体、抽样框以及纳入或排除个案的标准
senses.example: The research design names the population before the sample is drawn.
senses.exampleCN: 研究设计在抽取样本之前就写明总体。
senses.why: Who enters the study decides what the study can later say about the world, so selection belongs to the plan.
senses.whyCN: 谁进入研究决定了研究之后能对世界说什么，因此取样属于方案的一部分。

senses.title: The timing and sequence of measurement
senses.definition: the schedule of when data are collected, including cross-sectional or longitudinal choices
senses.definitionCN: 数据收集的时间安排，包括横断面或纵贯式的选择
senses.example: A longitudinal research design follows the same households for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 纵贯式研究设计追踪同一批家庭长达十年。
senses.why: Time is a design variable: measuring once and measuring repeatedly answer different questions.
senses.whyCN: 时间是设计变量：测一次与反复测回答的是不同的问题。

senses.title: The plan for instruments and measures
senses.definition: the selection and definition of questionnaires, tests, observation schedules or interview guides
senses.definitionCN: 选定并界定问卷、测验、观察记录表或访谈提纲
senses.example: The research design fixes the wording of every item in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 研究设计预先固定每个题项的字面表述。
senses.why: An instrument produces the numbers or texts a study will analyse, so its wording is part of the architecture.
senses.whyCN: 工具产生研究将要分析的数字或文本，因此它的措辞属于架构的一部分。

senses.title: The written protocol
senses.definition: the document that records procedures, materials and decision rules in enough detail for another team to repeat the work
senses.definitionCN: 把程序、材料与决策规则记录到另一支团队可以复做的详细文件
senses.example: Reviewers asked for the full research design as a separate document.
senses.exampleCN: 评审人要求把完整的研究设计作为单独文件提交。
senses.why: A plan that stays in someone's head cannot be reviewed, funded or repeated, so it is written down.
senses.whyCN: 留在个人脑子里的方案无法被评审、资助或复做，因此必须写成文件。

senses.title: The quality of the plan
senses.definition: the extent to which the plan protects internal and external validity against foreseeable threats
senses.definitionCN: 方案在可预见的威胁面前保护内部效度与外部效度的程度
senses.example: A weak research design cannot be repaired by a large sample.
senses.exampleCN: 薄弱的研究设计无法靠大样本补救。
senses.why: Design choices set the ceiling on what analysis can achieve, and later statistics can only work below that ceiling.
senses.whyCN: 设计选择给分析划定了上限，后来的统计只能在那个上限之下发挥作用。

intro.en: Research design joins a French word for close searching to a Latin word for marking out. The phrase itself is a modern social-science compound.
intro.cn: 这个术语把表示「仔细搜寻」的法语词与表示「划出标记」的拉丁词组合在一起，本身是现代社会科学的复合词。

items.en: Recerchier meant to search closely, built from an intensive prefix and cerchier, to search.
items.cn: 古法语 recerchier 意为仔细搜寻，由加强语气的前缀加 cerchier「搜寻」构成。

items.en: Cerchier descended from circare, to go about or wander, which came from circus, a circle.
items.cn: cerchier 源出 circare「四处走动、游走」，而 circare 又来自 circus「圆圈」。

items.en: English adopted research in the sixteenth century for close inquiry; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪引入 research 表示深入探究；确切的首见年代不确定。

items.en: Designare meant to mark out or designate, from de- out of and signum a sign.
items.cn: designare 意为划出、指定，由 de-「取出」加 signum「记号」构成。

items.en: French dess(e)in carried both drawing and intention, and English kept the plan and the purpose together.
items.cn: 法语 dess(e)in 同时带有「绘图」与「意图」，英语把方案与目的合在一起保留下来。

items.en: Statistics and the social sciences joined the two nouns into a name for the architecture of an inquiry.
items.cn: 统计学与社会科学把这两个名词组合成指研究架构的名称。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like this phrase; the second group names neighbouring ideas of planning and inquiry.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与本术语相近；第二组是与「规划、探究」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The first half, naming systematic inquiry.
entries.definitionCN: 前半，指系统的探究。

entries.definition: The second half, naming a plan or a marked-out arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 后半，指方案或划定的安排。

entries.definition: To mark out or name officially; it shares the Latin signum with design.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式指定或命名；与「设计」共享拉丁语 signum。

entries.definition: To plan again after the first plan has been tested.
entries.definitionCN: 指在初版方案受检验后重新规划。

entries.definition: Able to be investigated with available evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 指可以用现有证据加以探究的。

entries.definition: The study of methods and the reasoned system behind them.
entries.definitionCN: 指对方法的研究及其背后的理据体系。

entries.definition: A written procedure for carrying out a study.
entries.definitionCN: 指开展研究用的成文程序。

entries.definition: The part of a design that decides who will be studied.
entries.definitionCN: 指设计中决定研究谁的那一部分。

entries.definition: A controlled test arranged to reveal a causal relation.
entries.definitionCN: 指为揭示因果关系而安排的对照检验。

entries.definition: A structured collection of information from many respondents.
entries.definitionCN: 指从众多受访者处系统收集信息。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations work through the real parts, word family and common phrases behind this term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想依托这个术语背后真实的构词部件、同族词与常见搭配。

normal.en: Research and design are two ordinary words, and the phrase becomes technical only when they are joined.
normal.cn: 研究和设计都是普通词，只有组合起来才成为专业术语。

normal.en: The Latin signum behind design also gives designate and signal, so the word begins with a mark.
normal.cn: 「设计」背后的拉丁语 signum 也构成「指定」与「信号」两个词，这个词从「记号」开始。

normal.en: A design is approved before the study starts, just as a building plan is approved before the first brick.
normal.cn: 研究设计在开工前获批，正如建筑图纸在第一块砖之前获批。

normal.en: The word research carries the idea of searching again and again, not of finding once.
normal.cn: 研究一词带着反复搜寻的意思，而不是一次找到。

normal.en: Longitudinal, cross-sectional and experimental are the usual labels attached to a design.
normal.cn: 纵贯、横断面与实验是贴在研究设计上的常见标签。

abstract.en: A design is a promise made to future readers about what will count as evidence.
abstract.cn: 研究设计是对未来读者作出的承诺：什么才算证据。

abstract.en: The plan draws a fence around the study, and everything outside the fence is called a limitation.
abstract.cn: 方案在研究的四周画出围栏，围栏之外的一切后来都叫局限。

abstract.en: Two studies can use the same words and still differ entirely, because the architecture behind them differs.
abstract.cn: 两项研究可以用同样的词，却因背后的架构不同而完全不同。

examples.en: The team revised the research design after the pilot study.
examples.cn: 试点研究之后，团队修改了研究设计。

examples.en: A research design should state how missing data will be handled.
examples.cn: 研究设计应说明缺失数据将如何处理。

examples.en: The journal now asks authors to submit the research design with the manuscript.
examples.cn: 该期刊现在要求作者随稿提交研究设计。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「研究」加「设计」——先想清研究谁、测什么、何时停，再动手；图纸定得清楚，后面才不返工。

root: 古法语 recerchier「仔细搜寻」← 拉丁 circare「四处走动」← circus「圆圈」；拉丁 designare「划出、指定」← de-「取出」+ signum「记号」，经法语 design 进入英语；两词组合成现代研究术语。首见年代不确定不影响构词来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the whole plan to its parts: overall blueprint, strategy, comparison and control, sampling, timing, instruments, written protocol, and the quality of the plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从整体方案走向各部分：总体蓝图、策略选择、比较与控制、取样、时点、工具、成文方案，以及方案的严密程度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flow chart on a desk, with the research question at the top and branches for sample, measure, time and analysis.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上一张流程图，研究问题在顶端，向下分出样本、测量、时间与分析四支。

branches.en: THE WHOLE ARCHITECTURE: the plan that contains every later decision.
branches.cn: 整体架构：容纳后续所有决策的方案。

branches.en: THE DECLARED STRATEGY: the chosen method and the document that records it.
branches.cn: 已宣告的策略：选定的方法以及记录它的文件。

branches.en: THE BUILT CONTRAST: groups and controls arranged so that a cause can be tested.
branches.cn: 搭好的对照：通过分组与控制使因果得以检验。

branches.en: THE ENTRY AND MEASUREMENT RULES: who is studied and with which instruments.
branches.cn: 进入与测量规则：研究谁、用什么工具。

branches.en: THE SCHEDULE AND ITS STRENGTH: when measurement happens, and how well the plan resists threats.
branches.cn: 时点与强度：何时测量，以及方案抵御威胁的能力。

intro.en: The phrase is two complete English nouns joined by syntax, each with its own Latin or French history.
intro.cn: 这个短语是两个完整英语名词按句法组合，各自带着拉丁语或法语的历史。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies circare and circus for research, and signum plus designare for design; French supplies the two noun forms that English borrowed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语为前半提供 circare 与 circus，为后半提供 signum 与 designare；法语提供英语借入的两个名词形式。

items.example: The prefix makes the searching repeated rather than casual.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀让搜寻变成反复而非随意。

items.example: The verb supplies the activity half of research.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供 research 的活动义。

items.example: The circle image survives in the idea of covering ground.
items.exampleCN: 圆圈意象留在「跑遍各处」的意思里。

items.example: The shape is the earliest layer of the first half.
items.exampleCN: 这个形状是前半最早的一层。

items.example: Design begins with a visible mark on a surface.
items.exampleCN: 设计从表面上的可见记号开始。

items.example: The prefix moves the marking out onto a plan.
items.exampleCN: 前缀把标记动作推向一张平面。

items.structure: Latin verb from de- plus signum
items.example: The verb gives English both design and designate.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词给英语同时带来 design 与 designate。

items.example: It forms researcher and designer.
items.exampleCN: 它构成研究者与设计者。

items.example: It names the act of planning or inquiring.
items.exampleCN: 它指规划或探究这一活动。

items.example: The compound is younger than either of its parts.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词比它的两个部件都年轻。

由研究动词加表示施动者的词尾构成，义为「研究者」
由拉丁语 designare 经法语而来，义为「设计；方案」
由设计动词加表示施动者的词尾构成，义为「设计者」
由表示「重新」的前缀加设计动词构成，义为「重新设计」

definition_zh: 面试；采访；访谈；正式会谈；面谈（动词：面试；采访；访谈）
definition_en: a formal conversation in which one person asks another questions in order to obtain information, judge suitability or record experience
core_image: 桌两边各坐一人，桌上摊着简历、问题清单与录音笔，录音笔的红灯亮着
scene: 招聘季的会议室里，桌两边各坐一人，一边翻简历，一边按清单提问，录音笔亮着红灯。The committee will interview six candidates for the research post.
sceneCN: 这里指求职面试（第 1 个义项：为评估候选人而进行的正式面谈）；句意为委员会将为研究岗位面试六名候选人。图中可辨识物件：简历、问题清单、录音笔、姓名牌、茶杯。

pos.zh: 面试；采访；访谈；正式会谈
面试；采访；访谈；接受访谈

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示施动者的词尾构成，义为「面试官；采访者」
由该动词加表示受事者的词尾构成，义为「受访者；被面试者」
由该动词加动名词词尾构成，义为「面试或访谈活动」
由该动词加表示「以……为基础」的复合成分构成，义为「基于访谈的」

senses.title: A formal meeting to assess a candidate
senses.definition: a planned meeting in which an employer asks a candidate questions to judge suitability for a post
senses.definitionCN: 雇主通过有计划地提问来判断求职者是否适合某一岗位的会面
senses.example: The committee will interview six candidates for the research post.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会将为研究岗位面试六名候选人。
senses.why: The earliest sense is a meeting face to face, and hiring turned that meeting into a test of fit.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项是面对面会面，招聘把这种会面变成了对适配度的考察。

senses.title: A journalistic question-and-answer
senses.definition: a conversation in which a reporter questions a person in order to publish their account
senses.definitionCN: 记者向某人提问，以便公开其说法或观点的对话
senses.example: The reporter recorded the interview beside the flooded road.
senses.exampleCN: 记者在受淹的道路旁完成了这次采访并录音。
senses.why: Journalism needs a named source speaking in their own words, so the meeting becomes a published format.
senses.whyCN: 新闻业需要具名消息源用自己的话说话，于是这种会面成为一种发表格式。

senses.title: A research conversation with a purpose
senses.definition: a guided conversation used to collect qualitative data about experience, meaning or practice
senses.definitionCN: 为收集关于经验、意义或实践的非数值数据而进行的有引导的对话
senses.example: The study used a semi-structured interview to explore how nurses make triage decisions.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究用半结构化访谈探究护士如何做出分诊决定。
senses.why: A researcher needs the participant's own account rather than a fixed answer, so the interview becomes a data-collection instrument.
senses.whyCN: 研究者需要参与者自己的叙述而不是固定答案，于是访谈成为收集数据的工具。

senses.title: A formal diplomatic or official meeting
senses.definition: a scheduled meeting between officials or representatives for discussion rather than employment
senses.definitionCN: 官员或代表之间为讨论而非招聘而安排的会面
senses.example: The two ministers held a brief interview before the signing.
senses.exampleCN: 两位部长在签署前进行了简短会谈。
senses.why: The old sense of a meeting between people of rank survives in diplomacy, where the word means talk rather than a test.
senses.whyCN: 「身份相当者会面」的旧义在外交场合保留下来，那里指交谈而不是考核。

senses.title: To question someone formally
senses.definition: to ask a person questions in a planned conversation, whether for hiring, reporting or research
senses.definitionCN: 在计划的对话中向某人提问，无论用于招聘、报道还是研究
senses.example: Researchers interview each participant twice, once before and once after the training.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者对每位参与者访谈两次，一次在培训前，一次在培训后。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb because the meeting is an action performed by one side on the other.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词，因为这种会面是由一方对另一方实施的动作。

senses.title: To take part in an interview
senses.definition: to be the person answering questions in a formal conversation
senses.definitionCN: 在正式对话中作为回答提问的一方
senses.example: She was interviewed by two assistants who had never met the family.
senses.exampleCN: 她接受了两名从未见过这个家庭的助理的访谈。
senses.why: English allows the same verb for both roles, and context decides who is asking and who is answering.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许同一个动词用于双方，由语境决定谁提问、谁回答。

senses.title: The record of a conversation
senses.definition: the written or audio record produced by such a conversation and later analysed
senses.definitionCN: 由这类对话产生、随后被分析的书面或录音记录
senses.example: The interview runs to forty pages and was coded by two analysts.
senses.exampleCN: 这份访谈记录长达四十页，由两名分析员编码。
senses.why: Once a conversation is recorded it becomes an object that can be read, quoted and rechecked.
senses.whyCN: 对话一旦被记录，就成为可以阅读、引用与复核的对象。

senses.title: A screening or police questioning
senses.definition: a formal questioning by an authority to establish facts, identity or risk
senses.definitionCN: 由主管机关为查明事实、身份或风险而进行的正式询问
senses.example: The border officer conducted a short interview before allowing entry.
senses.exampleCN: 边检官员在准许入境前进行了简短讯问。
senses.why: The word keeps its neutral sense of a formal meeting, even when the purpose is control rather than conversation.
senses.whyCN: 这个词保留了「正式会面」的中性义，即使目的是管控而非交流。

intro.en: Interview comes from French entrevoir, to see each other, built on Latin inter between and videre to see. The noun first meant a meeting, then a question-and-answer.
intro.cn: 这个词来自法语 entrevoir「彼此见面」，由拉丁语 inter「之间」与 videre「看见」构成。名词最初指会面，后来才指问答。

items.en: Inter meant between or among, and it still marks the mutual direction of the meeting.
items.cn: inter 意为「在……之间」，至今标出这种会面的相互性。

items.en: Videre meant to see; sight is the oldest image inside the word.
items.cn: videre 意为「看见」，视觉是这个词里最古老的意象。

items.en: Entrevoir meant to see each other or catch sight of one another, not yet to question.
items.cn: entrevoir 意为彼此看见或瞥见对方，当时还没有提问的意思。

items.en: Entrevue named the meeting itself, and English borrowed it as a formal encounter.
items.cn: entrevue 指会面本身，英语借入时表示正式会见。

items.en: English extended the word to a planned conversation in which one side asks questions; the exact date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语把这个词扩展到一方提问的计划性对话；确切年代不确定。

items.en: Journalism and later social research made the interview a named format with its own rules and records.
items.cn: 新闻业与后来的社会研究使访谈成为一种有规则、有记录的固定形式。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like interview; the second group names neighbouring forms of formal questioning.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 interview 相近；第二组是与「正式提问」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The person who asks the questions.
entries.definitionCN: 提出问题的一方。

entries.definition: The person who answers the questions.
entries.definitionCN: 回答提问的一方。

entries.definition: Sight or opinion; it carries the same Latin seeing verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指景象或看法；带着同一个拉丁语「看见」动词。

entries.definition: To look at something again; it shares videre but not the mutual prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指再次查看；共享 videre 但不带「相互」前缀。

entries.definition: To come between; it looks close but its root is venire, to come.
entries.definitionCN: 指介入其间；形近但词根是 venire「来」。

entries.definition: Persistent and often coercive questioning by an authority.
entries.definitionCN: 指主管机关持续且常带强迫性的讯问。

entries.definition: An informal exchange with no fixed roles of questioner and answerer.
entries.definitionCN: 指没有固定问答角色的非正式交流。

entries.definition: A standard set of questions given to many people in the same form.
entries.definitionCN: 指以相同形式向许多人发放的一组标准问题。

entries.definition: A moderated discussion among several participants at once.
entries.definitionCN: 指由主持人引导的多人同时讨论。

entries.definition: The act of asking, without implying a formal format.
entries.definitionCN: 指提问行为，不暗示正式形式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations work through the real parts, word family and common phrases behind this term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想依托这个术语背后真实的构词部件、同族词与常见搭配。

normal.en: Inter- means between and view means see, so an interview begins as two people looking at each other.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「之间」，词根意为「看见」，所以「访谈」最初是两个人相互看见。

normal.en: The pair interviewer and interviewee marks the two chairs in the room.
normal.cn: 「面试官」与「受访者」这一对词标出房间里的两把椅子。

normal.en: A research interview is guided by an interview guide, while a job interview is guided by a person specification.
normal.cn: 研究访谈由访谈提纲引导，求职面试由岗位要求引导。

normal.en: The word covers hiring, reporting, research and border control because each is a formal meeting with questions.
normal.cn: 这个词覆盖招聘、报道、研究与边检，因为每一项都是有提问的正式会面。

normal.en: An interview transcript turns speech into lines that can be coded.
normal.cn: 访谈逐字稿把口语变成可编码的行。

abstract.en: An interview is a frame that decides which answers can appear, long before any answer is given.
abstract.cn: 访谈是一个框架，在任何回答出现之前就决定了哪些回答可能出现。

abstract.en: Two people sit facing each other, and the table between them holds the purpose of the meeting.
abstract.cn: 两人相对而坐，两人之间的桌子承载着这次会面的目的。

abstract.en: A recorded interview freezes a conversation so that it can be replayed, disputed and quoted.
abstract.cn: 录音访谈把对话冻结，使它可被重放、争议与引用。

examples.en: The interviewer explained the purpose before starting the interview.
examples.cn: 面试官在开始面试前说明了目的。

examples.en: Each interview was transcribed and checked by a second reader.
examples.cn: 每次访谈都被转写并由第二位读者核对。

examples.en: The panel will interview shortlisted applicants next week.
examples.cn: 评审组下周将面试入围的申请者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特」加「看」——两个人互相看见、彼此问答：求职叫面试，记者叫采访，研究者叫访谈。

root: 法语 entrevoir「彼此看见」← 拉丁 inter「之间」+ videre「看见」；名词 entrevue「会面」进入英语后，十六世纪起扩展为「有提问的正式对话」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from hiring to record: job interview, journalistic interview, research interview, official meeting, the verb of questioning, the verb of being questioned, the record, and authority screening.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从招聘走向记录：求职面试、新闻采访、研究访谈、正式会谈、提问动词、受访动词、访谈记录，以及主管机关的审查性讯问。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two chairs facing each other across a table, with a list of questions, a resume and a recorder between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：两把椅子隔着桌子相对，中间放着问题清单、简历与录音笔。

branches.en: THE ASSESSMENT MEETING: the same format used to judge a candidate or to check facts at a border.
branches.cn: 评估性会面：同一形式既用于判断候选人，也用于在边境核查事实。

branches.en: THE PUBLISHED ACCOUNT: a reporter's questions and the record that later becomes a source.
branches.cn: 公开发表的叙述：记者的提问，以及后来成为来源的记录。

branches.en: THE DATA CONVERSATION: a guided talk whose purpose is evidence about experience.
branches.cn: 数据性对话：目的在于取得经验证据的有引导交谈。

branches.en: THE OFFICIAL TALK: a meeting of rank where discussion replaces assessment.
branches.cn: 官方交谈：以讨论取代考核的身份对等会面。

branches.en: THE TWO ROLES OF THE VERB: one side asks, the other side answers.
branches.cn: 动词的两种角色：一方提问，另一方作答。

intro.en: The word is a French noun built on Latin parts, with English verb endings added later.
intro.cn: 这个词是用法语构词、拉丁语部件建成的名词，后来加上英语动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin inter and videre supply the meeting and the sight; French entrevoir and entrevue supply the noun; English -er and -ee name the two roles.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inter 与 videre 提供「会面」与「看见」，法语 entrevoir 与 entrevue 提供名词，英语 -er 与 -ee 命名两个角色。

items.example: It marks the mutual direction of the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 它标出会面的相互方向。

items.example: Sight is the oldest layer of the word.
items.exampleCN: 视觉是这个词最古老的一层。

items.structure: French verb from inter plus videre
items.example: The French verb names the first moment of the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语动词指会面的最初一刻。

items.example: English borrowed this noun as interview.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个名词借入为 interview。

items.example: The word widened from meeting to questioning.
items.exampleCN: 词义从会面扩展到提问。

items.example: It forms interviewer.
items.exampleCN: 它构成面试官或采访者。

items.example: It forms interviewee.
items.exampleCN: 它构成受访者。

items.example: It names the practice of conducting interviews.
items.exampleCN: 它指进行访谈这一活动。

items.example: It labels the common research format.
items.exampleCN: 它标出常见的研究访谈形式。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示施动者的词尾构成，义为「面试官；采访者」
由该动词加表示受事者的词尾构成，义为「受访者；被面试者」
由该动词加动名词词尾构成，义为「面试或访谈活动」
由该动词加表示「以……为基础」的复合成分构成，义为「基于访谈的」

definition_en: a research procedure in which behaviour, events or settings are watched and recorded systematically rather than reported afterwards
core_image: 教室后排坐着记录员，手里一张按时间段分格的观察表，窗台放着计时器
scene: 教室后排，记录员不开口，只按时间段在表格里画勾，孩子们的活动被一格一格记下。The study relies on the observation method to record how children share materials.
sceneCN: 这里指系统的观察法（第 1 个义项：以系统观看记录行为的研究方法）；句意为这项研究依靠观察法记录儿童如何分享材料。图中可辨识物件：观察表、计时器、铅笔、教室桌椅、积木。

collocations.phrase: the limits of the observation method

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 observare 经法语而来，义为「观察；遵守」
由观察动词加表示动作的名词尾构成，义为「观察」
由观察动词加表示施动者的词尾构成，义为「观察者」
由希腊语 methodos 经拉丁语而来，义为「方法」
由该名词加表示「学问」的词尾构成，义为「方法论」

senses.title: Systematic watching as a research procedure
senses.titleCN: 作为研究程序的系统观察
senses.definition: a planned procedure in which a trained observer watches behaviour and records it under fixed rules
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练的观察者按固定规则观看并记录行为的计划性程序
senses.example: The study relies on the observation method to record how children share materials.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究依靠观察法记录儿童如何分享材料。
senses.why: Watching becomes a method only when the time, place and categories of recording are decided in advance.
senses.whyCN: 只有当时间、地点与记录类别都预先确定，观看才成为方法。

senses.title: Participant observation
senses.definition: a form in which the researcher joins the setting and takes part in its ordinary activities while observing
senses.definitionCN: 研究者进入场景并参与日常活动，同时进行观察的形式
senses.example: The observation method can be participant, with the researcher joining the shift as a trainee.
senses.exampleCN: 观察法可以是参与式的，研究者以受训者身份加入班组。
senses.why: Some settings close themselves to outsiders, so access depends on becoming a member.
senses.whyCN: 有些场景对外人关闭，进入的代价就是先成为成员。

senses.title: Non-participant observation
senses.definition: a form in which the researcher stays outside the activity and watches without joining it
senses.definitionCN: 研究者留在活动之外观看而不加入的形式
senses.example: A non-participant observation method keeps the researcher outside the group.
senses.exampleCN: 非参与式观察法让研究者留在群体之外。
senses.why: Distance protects the setting from disturbance, but it also removes the observer from the participants' own meanings.
senses.whyCN: 距离使场景免受打扰，但也让观察者远离参与者自己的意义世界。

senses.title: Naturalistic observation
senses.definition: observation of behaviour in its ordinary setting, with as little interference as the research allows
senses.definitionCN: 在尽可能少干预的情况下，于日常情境中观察行为
senses.example: The observation method works best when the setting is left undisturbed.
senses.exampleCN: 当场景不受打扰时，观察法效果最好。
senses.why: If the aim is to know what people do when not watched, the setting must stay as it normally is.
senses.whyCN: 如果目的是了解人们不被观察时会怎么做，场景就必须维持原样。

senses.title: Structured observation
senses.definition: observation guided by a fixed checklist, category system or time sampling scheme
senses.definitionCN: 由固定清单、类别系统或时间抽样方案引导的观察
senses.example: A structured observation method uses a fixed checklist of categories.
senses.exampleCN: 结构化观察法使用固定的类别清单。
senses.why: Comparable records across observers require the same categories and the same sampling intervals.
senses.whyCN: 要让不同观察者的记录可比，就需要相同类别与相同时间间隔。

senses.title: Controlled or laboratory observation
senses.titleCN: 受控观察或实验室观察
senses.definition: observation arranged in a controlled setting so that conditions can be held constant
senses.definitionCN: 在受控场景中安排观察，使条件保持恒定
senses.example: The observation method may move into a laboratory when control is needed.
senses.exampleCN: 需要控制条件时，观察法可以移入实验室。
senses.why: Some behaviours are too brief or too rare to wait for in the field, so the setting is staged.
senses.whyCN: 有些行为太短或太罕见，在现场等不到，于是场景被安排出来。

senses.title: Classroom or clinical observation
senses.definition: the professional use of systematic watching to document participation, progress or symptoms
senses.definitionCN: 专业人员用系统观看记录参与度、进展或症状的做法
senses.example: Teachers use the observation method to document classroom participation.
senses.exampleCN: 教师用观察法记录课堂参与情况。
senses.why: Practice needs evidence that is not drawn from a single test score, so watching is written into routine records.
senses.whyCN: 实践需要不来自单次测验分数的证据，于是观看被写进日常记录。

senses.title: The limits of observation as evidence
senses.definition: the methodological problems of reactivity, observer drift, sampling of occasions and reliability
senses.definitionCN: 反应性、观察者漂移、情境取样与可靠性等方法问题
senses.example: The observation method is weakened when the observer's presence changes behaviour.
senses.exampleCN: 当观察者的在场改变行为时，观察法就被削弱。
senses.why: A method that records behaviour also becomes part of the situation it records, and that is its central weakness.
senses.whyCN: 记录行为的方法本身也成为被记录情境的一部分，这正是它的核心弱点。

intro.en: Observation method joins Latin observare, to watch or keep, to Greek methodos, a way of pursuit. The compound is a modern research label rather than an old word.
intro.cn: 这个术语把拉丁语 observare「观看、留意」与希腊语 methodos「追寻之路」组合起来，是现代研究标签而非古老词。

items.en: Observare meant to watch over, keep or pay attention to, built from ob- toward and servare to keep.
items.cn: observare 意为看守、留意、注意，由 ob-「朝向」加 servare「保持」构成。

items.en: Observatio named the act of watching and also the respect paid to a rule.
items.cn: observatio 既指观看行为，也指对规则的遵守。

items.en: English adopted observation for careful noticing; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语用 observation 表示仔细留意；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Methodos meant a way of pursuit, from meta after or along and hodos a road.
items.cn: methodos 意为追寻之路，由 meta「沿着」与 hodos「道路」构成。

items.en: Latin took the Greek word into learned usage, and English received method through French.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个希腊词带入学术用法，英语再经法语得到 method。

items.en: Social research joined the two nouns to name watching done under explicit rules.
items.cn: 社会科学把这两个名词组合，指在明确规则下进行的观看。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like observation method; the second group names neighbouring ways of studying a setting.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与本术语相近；第二组是与「研究场景」意思相邻的做法。

entries.definition: To watch or notice deliberately.
entries.definitionCN: 指有意观看或留意。

entries.definition: The person who watches and records.
entries.definitionCN: 指观看并记录的人。

entries.definition: The keeping of a rule or ritual, from the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指遵守规则或仪式，出自同一拉丁动词。

entries.definition: A planned way of doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 指有计划的做法。

entries.definition: The study of methods rather than a single method.
entries.definitionCN: 指对方法的研究，而非某一具体方法。

entries.definition: Long-term study of a group through immersion and field notes.
entries.definitionCN: 指通过长期沉浸与田野笔记研究一个群体。

entries.definition: Research carried out in the setting where the activity occurs.
entries.definitionCN: 指在活动发生的场景中开展的研究。

entries.definition: Repeated checking of conditions, often for management rather than research.
entries.definitionCN: 指反复检查状况，常为管理而非研究。

entries.definition: Detailed examination of one case or a few cases.
entries.definitionCN: 指对一个或少数个案的细致考察。

entries.definition: A fixed list of items used to standardise recording.
entries.definitionCN: 指用于统一记录的固定条目清单。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations work through the real parts, word family and common phrases behind this term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想依托这个术语背后真实的构词部件、同族词与常见搭配。

normal.en: The word begins with watching and ends with a road, which is exactly what a method is: a watched path.
normal.cn: 这个词以「观看」开头、以「道路」结尾，方法正是这样一条被看着的路。

normal.en: Participant and non-participant are the two chairs an observer may take.
normal.cn: 参与与非参与是观察者可以坐的两把椅子。

normal.en: A checklist turns watching into comparable ticks across observers.
normal.cn: 清单把观看变成不同观察者之间可比的勾选。

normal.en: Reactivity is the name for the change a watched person makes in response to being watched.
normal.cn: 反应性指被观察者因被观看而作出的改变。

normal.en: Observer drift is the slow change in how one person applies the same categories over time.
normal.cn: 观察者漂移指同一个人随着时间推移对相同类别的判定发生缓慢变化。

abstract.en: The observer is a measuring instrument that cannot be calibrated once and left alone.
abstract.cn: 观察者是一件无法一次校准就永久使用的测量仪器。

abstract.en: A method that watches people also teaches them how to be watched.
abstract.cn: 观看人的方法同时也在教他们如何被观看。

abstract.en: The record is not the event; it is the event after it has passed through one pair of eyes.
abstract.cn: 记录不是事件本身，而是事件穿过一双眼睛之后的样子。

examples.en: The observation method requires a clear definition of each behaviour category.
examples.cn: 观察法要求对每个行为类别给出清晰定义。

examples.en: She compared the observation method with interviews in the same classroom.
examples.cn: 她在同一间教室里比较了观察法与访谈。

examples.en: Training reduced observer drift in the observation method.
examples.cn: 培训减少了观察法中的观察者漂移。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「观察」加「方法」——看什么、何时看、怎么记，三件事定死，观看才变成研究。

root: 拉丁 observare「看守、留意」← ob-「朝向」+ servare「保持」，名词 observatio；希腊 methodos「追寻之路」← meta「沿着」+ hodos「道路」，经拉丁 methodus 与法语进入英语；两词组合为现代研究术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the general procedure to its variants and limits: systematic watching, participant and non-participant forms, naturalistic and structured observation, controlled settings, professional use, and methodological weaknesses.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一般程序走向各种形式与局限：系统观看、参与与非参与、自然情境与结构化、受控场景、专业应用，以及方法弱点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a recorder sits at the back of a room with a grid sheet divided by time intervals, ticking what happens in each cell.
core.cn: 核心意象：记录员坐在房间后排，手持按时间分格的表格，在每一格里勾下发生的事。

branches.en: THE PROCEDURE: watching turned into a method by prior rules.
branches.cn: 程序：通过预先规则把观看变成方法。

branches.en: THE TWO POSITIONS: inside the group or outside it.
branches.cn: 两种位置：群体之内或群体之外。

branches.en: THE SETTING: left undisturbed, or arranged for control.
branches.cn: 场景：保持原样，或为控制而布置。

branches.en: THE RECORDING PRACTICE: checklists for comparison, and routine professional documentation.
branches.cn: 记录实践：为比较而用清单，以及日常专业记录。

branches.en: THE WEAKNESS: the observer becomes part of what is observed.
branches.cn: 弱点：观察者成为被观察对象的一部分。

intro.en: The phrase is two complete words: a Latin-derived noun for watching and a Greek-derived noun for a way.
intro.cn: 这个短语是两个完整单词：拉丁来源的「观看」名词与希腊来源的「道路」名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies observare and servare for the first half, Greek supplies methodos and hodos for the second; English endings and compounding do the joining.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语为前半提供 observare 与 servare，希腊语为后半提供 methodos 与 hodos；英语词尾与复合构词完成连接。

items.example: It directs attention toward the object watched.
items.exampleCN: 它把注意力引向被观看的对象。

items.example: Watching is framed as keeping something under care.
items.exampleCN: 观看被框定为对某物的看守。

items.structure: Latin verb from ob- plus servare
items.example: The verb supplies the first half of the term.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供术语的前半。

items.example: The noun carries both attention and compliance.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时带有注意与遵守。

items.example: It marks pursuit along a path.
items.exampleCN: 它标出沿路追寻。

items.example: The second half begins with a road.
items.exampleCN: 后半从一条道路开始。

items.structure: Greek noun from meta plus hodos
items.example: The Greek word became Latin methodus and English method.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊词变成拉丁 methodus 与英语 method。

items.example: It forms methodological.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 methodological。

items.example: It forms observer.
items.exampleCN: 它构成观察者。

items.example: The compound is a modern research label.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是现代研究标签。

latinEntries.structure: methodus, methodi (f., second declension, from Greek methodos)

由观察动词加表示动作的名词尾构成，义为「观察」
由观察动词加表示施动者的词尾构成，义为「观察者」
由希腊语 methodos 经拉丁语而来，义为「方法」
由该名词加表示「学问」的词尾构成，义为「方法论」

definition_zh: 限制；约束；限制条件；约束力；强制
definition_en: a limit or restriction that reduces what a person, system or design may do, or the force that imposes such a limit
core_image: 四根拉索把箱体四角拴在台面夹具上，绳索绷紧，箱角留下勒痕
scene: 装配台上，四根拉索把箱体拴在夹具里，往任何一边推都会被绳子拽回原位。A tight budget is the main constraint on the project.
sceneCN: 这里指资源上的限制（第 3 个义项：时间、资金或人力不足造成的限制）；句意为紧张的预算是这个项目最主要的限制。图中可辨识物件：箱体、四根拉索、夹具、台面、勒痕。

pos.zh: 限制；约束；限制条件；约束力；强制

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 constringere 经法语而来，义为「限制；强迫」
由限制动词加已然词尾构成，义为「受限制的；勉强的」
由限制动词加现在分词词尾构成，义为「造成限制的」
由表示「向后」的前缀加同一拉丁词根构成，义为「抑制；约束」
由表示「共同」的前缀加同一拉丁词根构成，义为「压缩；收紧」

senses.title: A limit on what is possible
senses.definition: a condition that narrows the range of actions or outcomes available
senses.definitionCN: 缩小可选行动或结果范围的条件
senses.example: Funding is the constraint that decides the scope of the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 资金是决定试验规模的那个限制。
senses.why: The word begins with a rope pulled tight, and any limit draws the same boundary around action.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从一根绷紧的绳子开始，任何限制都在行动周围画出同样的边界。

senses.title: An imposed rule or condition
senses.definition: an external rule, permit condition or legal requirement that must be obeyed
senses.definitionCN: 必须遵守的外部规则、许可条件或法律要求
senses.example: The permit imposes a constraint on how much water may be drawn.
senses.exampleCN: 许可证对可取水量施加了一项限制。
senses.why: An authority binds behaviour by writing conditions, and the word names that binding.
senses.whyCN: 主管方用书面条件来绑定行为，这个词指的就是这种绑定。

senses.title: A shortage of time, money or staff
senses.definition: a practical scarcity that limits what a project can attempt within its resources
senses.definitionCN: 使项目在现有资源内只能做到某一步的现实短缺
senses.example: Time is the tightest constraint in the fieldwork season.
senses.exampleCN: 野外工作季里最紧的限制是时间。
senses.why: Resources are ropes of a different material: they pull the plan back whenever it tries to expand.
senses.whyCN: 资源是另一种材质的绳子：方案一想扩张，它就把方案拽回来。

senses.title: Physical restraint
senses.definition: a device or force that keeps a body or object from moving freely
senses.definitionCN: 使身体或物体无法自由移动的装置或力量
senses.example: A physical constraint kept the patient's arm from moving.
senses.exampleCN: 一项物理约束使病人的手臂无法移动。
senses.why: This is the literal sense: something is tied, and the tie is visible.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面义：某物被拴住，而拴住它的东西看得见。

senses.title: A condition in mathematics or optimization
senses.titleCN: 数学或优化中的约束条件
senses.definition: an equation or inequality that a solution must satisfy
senses.definitionCN: 求解结果必须满足的等式或不等式
senses.example: The model adds a constraint that total cost must stay below budget.
senses.exampleCN: 模型增加了一条约束：总成本必须低于预算。
senses.why: In optimization the search space is cut by conditions, and the solution exists only inside the cut.
senses.whyCN: 在优化中，条件把搜索空间切开，解只存在于切出的范围内。

senses.title: An engineering or design limit
senses.definition: a fixed limit on weight, size, temperature, cost or performance that a design must respect
senses.definitionCN: 设计在重量、尺寸、温度、成本或性能上必须遵守的固定界限
senses.example: Every design faces a constraint on weight and size.
senses.exampleCN: 每一项设计都面对重量与尺寸的限制。
senses.why: An engineer works between limits rather than in open space, and the limits are named as constraints.
senses.whyCN: 工程师是在界限之间而非空地上工作，这些界限就叫约束。

senses.title: Compulsion that forces action
senses.definition: pressure or obligation that leaves a person no acceptable alternative
senses.definitionCN: 使人别无合宜选择而只能照做的压力或义务
senses.example: A legal constraint compelled the firm to release the records.
senses.exampleCN: 一项法律强制力迫使该公司交出记录。
senses.why: A binding can also be applied to a person's will, not only to a body, and then it means compulsion.
senses.whyCN: 绳索也可以绑在人的意志上而不只是身体上，这时它指强制。

senses.title: A structural limit on freedom
senses.definition: a social, economic or institutional condition that restricts choices without any single visible rule
senses.definitionCN: 没有单一可见规则却限制选择的社会、经济或制度条件
senses.example: Social constraint can keep a group from questioning a familiar practice.
senses.exampleCN: 社会约束可以使一个群体不去质疑熟悉的做法。
senses.why: Some limits are not written anywhere yet still hold people in place, and the word covers those too.
senses.whyCN: 有些限制哪里都没写，却仍把人固定在原地，这个词也涵盖这些情况。

intro.en: Constraint comes from Latin constringere, to bind tightly, from con- together and stringere to draw tight. Old French passed the noun to English.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 constringere「紧紧捆绑」，由 con-「一起」与 stringere「拉紧」构成，经古法语名词进入英语。

items.en: Stringere meant to draw tight, to bind or to touch lightly; the rope image is original.
items.cn: stringere 意为拉紧、捆绑或轻触，绳索意象就是它的本义。

items.en: Con- added the idea of binding together, so the verb meant to squeeze or confine from all sides.
items.cn: con- 加入「捆在一起」的意思，这个动词于是指从四面挤压或收束。

items.en: The noun named a drawing together, whether of a rope, a wound or a rule.
items.cn: 名词指收束、紧缩，无论对象是绳索、伤口还是规则。

items.en: Old French kept the verb for compulsion and restraint, and the noun constreinte followed.
items.cn: 古法语保留了这个动词的强迫与约束义，名词 constreinte 随之出现。

items.en: English borrowed the noun for a restriction or a forced condition; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语借入这个名词表示限制或被迫的条件；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Engineering, law and optimization each gave the word a precise local meaning without changing the rope image.
items.cn: 工程、法律与优化各自赋予这个词精确的局部含义，却没有改变绳索意象。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like constraint; the second group names neighbouring ideas of limiting and pressure.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 constraint 相近；第二组是与「限制、压力」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to limit or force.
entries.definitionCN: 指限制或强迫的动词。

entries.definition: Held within limits, or forced into an unnatural manner.
entries.definitionCN: 指受限于界限之内，或被逼得不自然。

entries.definition: A holding back; it uses the same Latin stringere with a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指抑制；用同一个拉丁词根但前缀不同。

entries.definition: To squeeze or narrow, often of a passage or a muscle.
entries.definitionCN: 指挤压或收窄，常用于通道或肌肉。

entries.definition: To pull or stretch tightly, and the resulting injury or effort.
entries.definitionCN: 指拉紧、拉伸，以及由此产生的损伤或用力。

entries.definition: A general boundary on what may be done.
entries.definitionCN: 指对可做之事的一般界限。

entries.definition: An official rule that limits action.
entries.definitionCN: 指限制行动的正式规定。

entries.definition: Something that stands in the way of progress.
entries.definitionCN: 指阻碍进展的事物。

entries.definition: Force applied to make someone act in a certain way.
entries.definitionCN: 指为使人按某种方式行动而施加的力量。

entries.definition: A condition that must be satisfied and cannot be ignored.
entries.definitionCN: 指必须满足、不可忽略的条件。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations work through the real parts, word family and common phrases behind this term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想依托这个术语背后真实的构词部件、同族词与常见搭配。

normal.en: The Latin verb means to tie tight, so every constraint begins as a rope around something.
normal.cn: 拉丁动词意为紧紧拴住，因此每一种约束最初都是绕在某物上的一根绳。

normal.en: Time, budget and staff are the three ropes that most often pull a project back.
normal.cn: 时间、预算与人手是最常把项目拽回的三根绳。

normal.en: A constraint in a model is an equation the answer must satisfy.
normal.cn: 模型中的约束是答案必须满足的一条等式。

normal.en: Constrained and restraint share the same root but different prefixes, one binding with, one holding back.
normal.cn: 「受限制的」与「抑制」共享词根但前缀不同，一个是捆在一起，一个是往回拉住。

normal.en: An engineering constraint is written into the specification before the first part is made.
normal.cn: 工程约束在第一个零件做出之前就写进规格书。

abstract.en: A constraint is a wall that does not need to be seen to be felt.
abstract.cn: 约束是一堵不必看见也能感觉到的墙。

abstract.en: Every free choice is drawn on a map whose edges were set by someone else.
abstract.cn: 每一次自由选择都画在一张由别人定好边界的地图上。

abstract.en: The tighter the rope, the clearer the shape; limits can make a design legible.
abstract.cn: 绳拉得越紧，形状越清楚；限制反而能让设计变得可读。

examples.en: The team treated cost as a constraint rather than a variable.
examples.cn: 团队把成本当作约束而非变量。

examples.en: A constraint on the sample size limited how many subgroups could be compared.
examples.cn: 样本量的限制决定了能比较多少个子组。

examples.en: The court's constraint required the company to change its disclosure practice.
examples.cn: 法院的强制要求迫使公司改变披露做法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「困住」的音——四根绳子把箱子困在台上，时间、预算、人力也这样把计划困住：约束、限制。

root: 拉丁 constringere「捆紧」← con-「一起」+ stringere「拉紧」；名词经古法语 constreinte 进入英语，本义为捆绑，后扩展到规则、资源、数学条件与强制。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the rope outward: a general limit, an imposed rule, resource scarcity, physical restraint, a mathematical condition, an engineering limit, compulsion, and a structural limit on freedom.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从绳子向外扩展：一般限制、外加规定、资源短缺、身体约束、数学条件、工程界限、强制力，以及对自由的结构性束缚。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four ropes pull a box tight against a fixture, so that every push is answered by a pull back.
core.cn: 核心意象：四根绳把箱体紧紧拉在夹具上，任何一推都会被一拉回应。

branches.en: THE PRACTICAL BOUNDARY: a general limit and the scarcity of time or money.
branches.cn: 现实边界：一般限制与时间、资金的短缺。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN BINDING: a rule or permit condition that must be obeyed.
branches.cn: 书面绑定：必须遵守的规则或许可条件。

branches.en: THE LITERAL RESTRAINT: a body or object physically held.
branches.cn: 字面约束：身体或物体被物理地固定。

branches.en: THE TECHNICAL LIMIT: conditions inside a model and limits inside a design.
branches.cn: 技术界限：模型内的条件与设计内的界限。

branches.en: THE PRESSURE ON WILL AND SOCIAL POSITION: compulsion, and unwritten structural limits.
branches.cn: 对意志与处境的压力：强制，以及未写明的结构性限制。

intro.en: Constraint is a Latin-derived noun whose stem also appears in restraint, constrict and strain.
intro.cn: 这是一个拉丁来源名词，其词干也出现在「抑制」「压缩」与「拉紧」三个词中。

latinIntro.en: Latin stringere supplies the tight rope; con- supplies the binding together; French supplies the noun form. The same root appears in several English words with different prefixes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stringere 提供绷紧的绳索，con- 提供捆在一起的动作，法语提供名词形式；同一词根以不同前缀出现在多个英语词中。

items.example: It makes the pulling a binding from all sides.
items.exampleCN: 它使拉紧成为从四面进行的捆绑。

items.example: The rope image is the oldest layer.
items.exampleCN: 绳索意象是最早的一层。

items.structure: Latin verb from con- plus stringere
items.example: The verb supplies the whole English family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供整个英语词族。

items.example: The noun named a tightened state.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指被收紧的状态。

items.structure: noun ending in the French form
items.example: The ending turns the verb into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 词尾把动词变成状态名词。

items.example: English widened the noun to rules and resources.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个名词扩展到规则与资源。

items.example: The verb keeps the active side of the image.
items.exampleCN: 动词保留意象中主动的一面。

items.example: It forms constrained.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 constrained。

items.example: It forms constraining.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 constraining。

items.structure: English noun with re- plus stringere
items.example: The re- prefix reverses the direction of the pull.
items.exampleCN: re- 前缀把拉的方向反过来。

definition_zh: 抽样偏差；抽样偏倚；样本偏差
definition_en: a systematic distortion in a sample because some members of the population are more likely to be included than others
core_image: 漏斗口偏向箱子一角，倒进去的球只从一边滚落，另一侧始终空着
scene: 抽奖箱的出口装在左角，摇一摇，球只从左边滚出来，右边堆着的一层始终没动。Sampling bias appears when the chosen group never resembles the wider population.
sceneCN: 这里指样本构成系统性偏离总体（第 1 个义项：因纳入机会不均造成的样本偏差）；句意为当被选中的群体与更大总体始终不像时，就出现了抽样偏差。图中可辨识物件：漏斗、出口、球、箱子、左右两侧的空地与堆积。

pos.zh: 抽样偏差；抽样偏倚；样本偏差

collocations.zh: 网络投票中的抽样偏差

derivatives.zh: 由古法语 essample 经拉丁语 exemplum 而来，义为「样本；抽样」
由抽样动词加动名词词尾构成，义为「抽样过程」
由古法语 biais「斜线」而来，义为「偏差；使有偏差」，更早来源不确定
由偏差动词加已然词尾构成，义为「有偏差的」
由抽样动词加表示施动者的词尾构成，义为「抽样者；采样器」

senses.title: A systematic distortion in who is included
senses.titleCN: 纳入机会不均造成的系统性偏差
senses.definition: a distortion that arises because inclusion probabilities differ across members of the population
senses.definitionCN: 因总体各成员的入选概率不同而产生的失真
senses.example: Sampling bias appears when the chosen group never resembles the wider population.
senses.exampleCN: 当被选中的群体与更大总体始终不像时，抽样偏差就出现了。
senses.why: The problem is not a wrong answer from one person but a wrong rule about who gets asked.
senses.whyCN: 问题不在于某一个人答错，而在于「谁被问到」的规则本身出错。

senses.title: An incomplete sampling frame
senses.titleCN: 抽样框不完整造成的偏差
senses.definition: distortion caused by a list or frame that leaves out parts of the population before selection begins
senses.definitionCN: 在抽取开始之前，名单或抽样框已经漏掉总体某些部分所造成的失真
senses.example: Sampling bias can begin with an incomplete list of households.
senses.exampleCN: 抽样偏差可能从一份不完整的住户名单开始。
senses.why: If a group never appears on the list, no amount of random selection from that list can reach it.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个群体根本不在名单上，从名单里再怎么随机抽取也到不了它。

senses.title: Self-selection bias
senses.definition: distortion produced when people decide for themselves whether to take part
senses.definitionCN: 由人们自行决定是否参加而产生的失真
senses.example: Internet polls often show sampling bias because volunteers choose themselves.
senses.exampleCN: 网络投票常有抽样偏差，因为参与者是自己选择加入的。
senses.why: Those with a strong opinion are more likely to volunteer, so the sample fills with one kind of person.
senses.whyCN: 意见强烈的人更可能自愿参与，样本于是被某一类人填满。

senses.title: Convenience sampling bias
senses.definition: distortion caused by choosing the easiest available cases rather than a representative selection
senses.definitionCN: 因选择最容易接触到而非有代表性的个案而产生的失真
senses.example: A mall survey carries sampling bias toward people who shop there.
senses.exampleCN: 商场问卷会对在那里购物的人产生抽样偏差。
senses.why: Convenience decides access, and access decides who can appear in the data.
senses.whyCN: 便利决定接触机会，接触机会决定谁能够出现在数据里。

senses.title: Survivorship bias
senses.definition: distortion that arises when only successful, surviving or still-present cases remain visible
senses.definitionCN: 只有成功、存活或仍在场的个案可见时产生的失真
senses.example: Survivorship bias is a form of sampling bias that hides failures.
senses.exampleCN: 幸存者偏差是抽样偏差的一种，它把失败者藏了起来。
senses.why: The absent cases carry the evidence that would change the conclusion, and absence removes them from the sample.
senses.whyCN: 缺席的个案带着能改变结论的证据，而缺席把它们从样本中移除了。

senses.title: Non-response bias
senses.definition: distortion produced when those who refuse or cannot answer differ systematically from those who do
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝回答或无法回答的人与回答者存在系统差异而产生的失真
senses.example: Sampling bias appears when those who refuse differ from those who answer.
senses.exampleCN: 当拒答者与回答者不同时，抽样偏差就出现了。
senses.why: A high response rate is not automatically safe; the question is whether the missing people are like the rest.
senses.whyCN: 高应答率并不自动安全，关键在于缺席者是否与其余人相似。

senses.title: Its effect on estimates
senses.definition: the shift in estimates and the loss of generalisability caused by a non-representative sample
senses.definitionCN: 非代表性样本造成的估计偏移与推广能力丧失
senses.example: Sampling bias makes the estimate shift even when the instrument is sound.
senses.exampleCN: 即使测量工具可靠，抽样偏差仍会使估计发生偏移。
senses.why: A good instrument applied to the wrong group produces a precise number about the wrong population.
senses.whyCN: 好工具用错了群体，只会得到关于错误总体的精确数字。

senses.title: Detection and correction
senses.definition: the comparison of sample and population profiles, plus weighting or redesign used to reduce the distortion
senses.definitionCN: 比较样本与总体轮廓，并用加权或重新设计来减少失真
senses.example: Weighting can reduce sampling bias but cannot restore missing groups.
senses.exampleCN: 加权可以减少抽样偏差，却无法把缺失的群体补回来。
senses.why: Correction can rebalance what was included, but it cannot invent evidence from people never reached.
senses.whyCN: 校正可以重新平衡已纳入的部分，却无法凭空造出从未接触到的人的证据。

intro.en: Sampling bias joins sample, from Latin exemplum through Old French, to bias, from Old French biais, a slant. The deeper origin of bias is uncertain and often treated as a borrowed Mediterranean term.
intro.cn: 这个术语把经古法语来自拉丁语 exemplum 的 sample，与来自古法语 biais「斜线」的 bias 组合起来；bias 更早的来源不确定，常被视为借自地中海一带的词。

items.en: Exemplum meant something taken out as a specimen, from eximere, to take out.
items.cn: exemplum 指取出作为样品的东西，来自 eximere「取出」。

items.en: Essample carried the sense of a specimen or a case, and English shortened it to sample.
items.cn: essample 带有「标本、实例」的意思，英语缩略为 sample。

items.en: English used sample for a part chosen to represent a whole; the modern statistical sense is later.
items.cn: 英语用 sample 指被选来代表整体的一部分，现代统计学义更晚。

items.en: Biais meant a slant or an oblique line, and the noun entered English as bias.
items.cn: biais 意为斜面或斜线，名词进入英语为 bias。

items.en: The origin of biais is source uncertain; one common proposal links it to a Greek word for slanted, but no direct chain is proven.
items.cn: biais 的更早来源不确定；一种常见说法把它联系到希腊语表示「倾斜」的词，但没有得到证实的直接链条。

items.en: Statistics used bias for a systematic departure from truth, and sampling bias names the departure caused by selection.
items.cn: 统计学用 bias 指对真相的系统性偏离，sampling bias 则指由选择造成的那种偏离。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like sampling bias; the second group names neighbouring kinds of statistical distortion.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 sampling bias 相近；第二组是与「统计失真」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The subset chosen from a population.
entries.definitionCN: 指从总体中选出的子集。

entries.definition: The process of choosing that subset.
entries.definitionCN: 指选择该子集的过程。

entries.definition: A systematic slant away from the true value.
entries.definitionCN: 指系统性地偏离真值。

entries.definition: Affected by such a slant.
entries.definitionCN: 指受这种偏离影响的。

entries.definition: A person or device that draws samples.
entries.definitionCN: 指抽样的人或采样装置。

entries.definition: Distortion from the rule that decides who enters the study.
entries.definitionCN: 指由决定谁进入研究的规则造成的失真。

entries.definition: Distortion from differences between responders and non-responders.
entries.definitionCN: 指回答者与未回答者之间的差异造成的失真。

entries.definition: The frame omits part of the population.
entries.definitionCN: 指抽样框遗漏了总体的一部分。

entries.definition: Adjusting records so that the sample profile matches the population.
entries.definitionCN: 指调整记录使样本轮廓与总体一致。

entries.definition: Any difference between an estimate and the true value, whether systematic or random.
entries.definitionCN: 指估计与真值之间的任何差异，无论系统或随机。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations work through the real parts, word family and common phrases behind this term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想依托这个术语背后真实的构词部件、同族词与常见搭配。

normal.en: Sample comes from a word for a specimen taken out, and bias from a word for a slant.
normal.cn: 「样本」来自「取出的标本」，「偏差」来自「斜线」。

normal.en: A sample that is chosen by volunteers is a sample of volunteers, not of the public.
normal.cn: 由志愿者组成的样本是志愿者的样本，不是公众的样本。

normal.en: An incomplete list is already a biased frame before any random draw happens.
normal.cn: 不完整的名单在随机抽取之前就已经是有偏差的抽样框。

normal.en: Survivorship bias keeps the winners visible and hides the failures.
normal.cn: 幸存者偏差让赢家可见，把失败者藏起来。

normal.en: Weighting adjusts the balance of what was collected, not the absence of what was missed.
normal.cn: 加权调整的是已收集部分的平衡，而不是缺失部分的补全。

abstract.en: A sample is a small mirror held up to a large room, and a warped mirror changes the room.
abstract.cn: 样本是一面举向大房间的小镜子，镜子一歪，房间也跟着变样。

abstract.en: Every inclusion rule is also an exclusion rule, and the exclusion is where the distortion enters.
abstract.cn: 每一条纳入规则同时也是一条排除规则，失真就从排除处进入。

abstract.en: The missing cases are the loudest part of the data, because they never make a sound.
abstract.cn: 缺失的个案是数据中最响的部分，因为它们从不发出声音。

examples.en: The report attributed the gap to sampling bias rather than to the questionnaire.
examples.cn: 报告把差距归因于抽样偏差，而不是问卷本身。

examples.en: Random selection reduces sampling bias but does not remove every source of it.
examples.cn: 随机抽取能减少抽样偏差，但不能消除它的所有来源。

examples.en: The authors tested for sampling bias by comparing the sample with census figures.
examples.cn: 作者通过把样本与普查数字比较来检验抽样偏差。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抽样」加「斜」——抽出来的那一小把总是偏向某一边，样本就歪了：抽样偏差。

root: 拉丁 exemplum「取出的样品」← eximere「取出」，经古法语 essample 进入英语为 sample；古法语 biais「斜线」进入英语为 bias，更早来源不确定，常被联系到希腊语「倾斜」但无证实链条；统计学把二者组合为 sampling bias。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the general distortion to its mechanisms and treatment: selection distortion, incomplete frames, self-selection, convenience access, survivorship, non-response, effects on estimates, and detection or correction.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一般失真走向具体机制与处理：选择失真、抽样框不全、自选、便利接触、幸存者、无应答、对估计的影响，以及识别与校正。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a funnel tilted to one corner, so that all the balls roll out on one side and the other side stays empty.
core.cn: 核心意象：漏斗歪向一角，所有球都从一边滚出，另一边始终空着。

branches.en: THE DEFINITION: inclusion probabilities differ, so the sample is systematically unlike the population.
branches.cn: 定义：入选概率不均，样本因此系统性不像总体。

branches.en: THE FRAME FAILURE: the list itself leaves people out before selection starts.
branches.cn: 抽样框失效：名单在抽取之前就把人漏掉。

branches.en: THE VOLUNTARY AND CONVENIENT ENTRY: people choose themselves in, or the researcher chooses whoever is easy to reach.
branches.cn: 自愿与便利进入：人们自己选择加入，或研究者选择容易接触到的人。

branches.en: THE INVISIBLE AND THE SILENT: survivors stay visible and refusers stay unheard.
branches.cn: 不可见者与沉默者：幸存者留在视野里，拒答者不被听见。

branches.en: THE ESTIMATE AND THE REMEDY: a precise number about the wrong group, and correction that cannot restore the missing.
branches.cn: 估计与补救：关于错误群体的精确数字，以及无法补回缺失者的校正。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin-derived noun for a specimen to a French-derived noun for a slant.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁来源的「样品」名词与法语来源的「斜线」名词组合起来。

latinIntro.en: Latin exemplum and eximere supply sample; Old French biais supplies bias, with a deeper origin that is uncertain. The statistical compound is modern.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 exemplum 与 eximere 提供前半，古法语 biais 提供后半，其更早来源不确定；统计学的复合用法是现代产物。

items.example: It marks taking something out of a larger set.
items.exampleCN: 它标出从更大集合中取出某物。

items.example: The root supplies the taking in eximere.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供 eximere 中「拿取」的意思。

items.example: French and English shortened it toward sample.
items.exampleCN: 法语与英语把它简化为 sample。

items.structure: English noun from Old French essample
items.example: The first half names what is selected.
items.exampleCN: 前半命名被选出的部分。

items.example: The second half begins as a physical slope.
items.exampleCN: 后半从一条物理斜面开始。

items.meaning: a leaning away from the true value
items.example: The physical slope became a statistical slant.
items.exampleCN: 物理斜面变成了统计斜线。

items.example: It forms sampling.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 sampling。

items.example: The first half becomes a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 前半变成过程名词。

items.meaning: distortion caused by the selection rule
items.meaningCN: 由选择规则造成的失真
items.example: The compound names a mechanism, not a single careless mistake.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指一种机制，而不是一次粗心错误。

derivatives.zh: 由古法语 essample 经拉丁语 exemplum 而来，义为「样本；抽样」
由抽样动词加动名词词尾构成，义为「抽样过程」
由古法语 biais「斜线」而来，义为「偏差；使有偏差」，更早来源不确定
由偏差动词加已然词尾构成，义为「有偏差的」
由抽样动词加表示施动者的词尾构成，义为「抽样者；采样器」

definition_en: systematic distortion in an experiment caused by the way participants are chosen, treated, measured or observed, rather than by the treatment itself
core_image: 实验者先在记录表上画下预期箭头，受试者进门看见门上的分组牌，回答明显向箭头方向靠
scene: 实验室里，助手把分组名单贴在门上，受试者进门先看到牌子，作答时明显往预期方向靠。Experimental bias can enter through a posted sign as easily as through a faulty scale.
sceneCN: 这里指实验者期望造成的偏差（第 1 个义项：实验者的预期影响结果）；句意为一纸贴在门上的分组牌，和一台失准的秤一样，都能把实验偏差带进来。图中可辨识物件：分组牌、记录表、预期箭头、受试者、量表。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 experimentum「试验」而来，义为「实验」
由该名词加形容词词尾构成，义为「实验的」
由该名词加表示施动者的词尾构成，义为「实验者」
由古法语 biais「斜线」而来，义为「偏差」，更早来源不确定
由偏差动词加已然词尾构成，义为「有偏差的」
由否定前缀加有偏差的形容词构成，义为「无偏差的」

senses.title: Experimenter expectancy
senses.definition: distortion produced when an experimenter's hypothesis subtly shapes how participants are treated or how responses are read
senses.definitionCN: 实验者的假设在不知不觉中影响对待方式或判读方式而产生的失真
senses.example: Experimental bias can enter through a posted sign as easily as through a faulty scale.
senses.exampleCN: 实验偏差可以像失准的秤一样，轻易地从一张贴出的牌子进入。
senses.why: A person who expects a result may speak, gesture or score in ways that help the result appear.
senses.whyCN: 期待某个结果的人，可能用说话、手势或评分方式帮助那个结果出现。

senses.title: Participant response bias
senses.definition: distortion produced when participants guess what the study wants and answer in that direction
senses.definitionCN: 受试者猜测研究想要什么并朝那个方向作答而产生的失真
senses.example: Participants who read the study aim may introduce experimental bias into their own ratings.
senses.exampleCN: 读到研究目的的受试者可能把实验偏差带进自己的评分。
senses.why: Being observed is itself a treatment, and the participant's interpretation of the setting becomes part of the response.
senses.whyCN: 被观察本身即是一种处理，受试者对场景的理解成为回答的一部分。

senses.title: Selection and assignment bias
senses.definition: distortion caused by non-random assignment that puts different kinds of people into different groups
senses.definitionCN: 非随机分组把不同类型的人放进不同组而产生的失真
senses.example: Assignment by convenience can create experimental bias before the treatment begins.
senses.exampleCN: 按便利分组会在处理开始之前就造成实验偏差。
senses.why: If the groups differ at the start, a later difference cannot be credited to the treatment.
senses.whyCN: 如果各组在开始时就有差异，后来的差异就不能归给处理。

senses.title: Confounding by an uncontrolled variable
senses.titleCN: 未受控变量造成的混杂
senses.definition: distortion produced when another variable changes together with the treatment and could explain the result
senses.definitionCN: 另一个变量与处理同时变化、并可能解释结果而产生的失真
senses.example: A change in room temperature became a source of experimental bias in the reaction trial.
senses.exampleCN: 室温变化成了反应试验中实验偏差的一个来源。
senses.why: The experiment holds one cause in view, but a second cause moves at the same time and takes the credit.
senses.whyCN: 实验盯住一个原因，第二个原因却同时移动并领走了功劳。

senses.title: Measurement and instrument bias
senses.definition: distortion produced by a poorly calibrated, insensitive or inconsistently read instrument
senses.definitionCN: 仪器未校准、不够灵敏或读数不一致而产生的失真
senses.example: The scale introduced experimental bias because it had not been zeroed.
senses.exampleCN: 那台秤没有归零，因而引入了实验偏差。
senses.why: A tool that leans consistently to one side is not noisy; it is biased, and more trials will not fix it.
senses.whyCN: 总是往一侧偏的工具不是噪声，而是有偏差，多测几次也修不好。

senses.title: Procedure and order effects
senses.definition: distortion produced by the order of tasks, learning, fatigue or carry-over between conditions
senses.definitionCN: 任务顺序、学习、疲劳或条件间残留影响而产生的失真
senses.example: Counterbalancing is used to keep order effects from becoming experimental bias.
senses.exampleCN: 使用顺序平衡，是为了避免顺序效应变成实验偏差。
senses.why: The second condition is never a clean repeat of the first, because the first has already happened.
senses.whyCN: 第二个条件永远不是第一个的干净重复，因为第一个已经发生过。

senses.title: Analysis and reporting bias
senses.definition: distortion produced by choosing favourable outcomes, models or subgroups after the data have been seen
senses.definitionCN: 在看到数据之后挑选有利结果、模型或子组而产生的失真
senses.example: Reporting only the significant subgroup added experimental bias to the published result.
senses.exampleCN: 只报告显著的子组，给已发表的结果添上了实验偏差。
senses.why: The data are fixed, but the analyst's freedom to choose a summary turns an honest trial into a selected story.
senses.whyCN: 数据是固定的，但分析者选择摘要方式的自由，会把诚实的试验变成挑选过的故事。

senses.title: Blinding and randomisation as remedies
senses.titleCN: 盲法与随机化作为对策
senses.definition: the design practices that keep expectancy, assignment and measurement from entering the result
senses.definitionCN: 防止期望、分组与测量进入结果的设计做法
senses.example: Double-blind trials are the standard defence against experimental bias.
senses.exampleCN: 双盲试验是防范实验偏差的标准做法。
senses.why: If neither side knows the condition, expectation loses the information it needs to act.
senses.whyCN: 当双方都不知道分组时，期望就失去了它可以用来起作用的信息。

intro.en: Experimental bias joins experiment, from Latin experimentum, a trial, to bias, from Old French biais, a slant whose deeper origin is uncertain. The phrase is modern.
intro.cn: 这个术语把来自拉丁语 experimentum「试验」的 experiment，与来自古法语 biais「斜线」的 bias 组合起来；bias 更早的来源不确定。整个短语是现代用法。

items.en: Experiri meant to try or to put to the test, built from ex- out and periri to attempt.
items.cn: experiri 意为尝试、考验，由 ex-「取出」与 periri「尝试」构成。

items.en: Experimentum named a trial or a proof, and English took it as experiment.
items.cn: experimentum 指试验或证明，英语借入为 experiment。

items.en: The adjective experimental appeared with the growth of controlled science; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 形容词 experimental 随受控科学的发展而出现；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Biais meant a slant or an oblique line, and English borrowed it as bias.
items.cn: biais 意为斜面或斜线，英语借入为 bias。

items.en: The origin of biais is source uncertain; a Greek link has been proposed but not proven.
items.cn: biais 的更早来源不确定；有人提出与希腊语有关，但未获证实。

items.en: Statistical method made bias a technical term for systematic departure from truth, and the compound names the experimental sources of it.
items.cn: 统计方法使 bias 成为「系统性偏离真相」的技术术语，这个复合词则命名实验中的各种来源。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like experimental bias; the second group names neighbouring threats to a valid experiment.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 experimental bias 相近；第二组是与「实验效度威胁」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: A controlled trial designed to test a claim.
entries.definitionCN: 指为检验某一主张而安排的对照试验。

entries.definition: Relating to such a trial.
entries.definitionCN: 指与这类试验有关的。

entries.definition: The person who runs the trial.
entries.definitionCN: 指执行试验的人。

entries.definition: A systematic slant away from the true value.
entries.definitionCN: 指系统性地偏离真值。

entries.definition: Affected by such a slant.
entries.definitionCN: 指受这种偏离影响的。

entries.definition: Mixing of the treatment with another cause so that the two cannot be separated.
entries.definitionCN: 指处理与另一原因混在一起而无法分开。

entries.definition: Cues that tell participants what the study expects.
entries.definitionCN: 指告诉受试者研究期待什么的线索。

entries.definition: Distortion in what an observer notices and records.
entries.definitionCN: 指观察者注意与记录内容上的失真。

entries.definition: Assignment by random chance, used to balance unknown differences.
entries.definitionCN: 指按随机方式分组，以平衡未知差异。

entries.definition: Change produced by expectation rather than by the treatment.
entries.definitionCN: 指由期待而非处理造成的变化。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations work through the real parts, word family and common phrases behind this term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想依托这个术语背后真实的构词部件、同族词与常见搭配。

normal.en: Experiment comes from a word for trial, and bias from a word for slant, so the phrase names a trial that leans.
normal.cn: 「实验」来自「试验」，「偏差」来自「斜线」，这个短语指一场歪着的试验。

normal.en: The four entries for bias are the experimenter, the participant, the assignment and the instrument.
normal.cn: 实验偏差的四个入口是实验者、受试者、分组与仪器。

normal.en: Double-blind means neither the participant nor the person scoring knows the condition.
normal.cn: 双盲指受试者与评分者都不知道分组。

normal.en: A confound is a second cause travelling with the treatment.
normal.cn: 混杂是跟处理一起同行的第二个原因。

normal.en: Counterbalancing changes the order so that order itself cannot explain the difference.
normal.cn: 顺序平衡改变任务次序，使次序本身无法解释差异。

abstract.en: An experiment is a question asked of nature, and bias is the accent of the person asking.
abstract.cn: 实验是向自然提出的问题，偏差是提问者的口音。

abstract.en: The cleanest trial is one in which the people who know the answer are kept away from the people who give it.
abstract.cn: 最干净的试验，是让知道答案的人远离给出答案的人。

abstract.en: A result that favours the hypothesis may be evidence, or it may be the hypothesis looking at itself.
abstract.cn: 支持假设的结果可能是证据，也可能是假设在照镜子。

examples.en: The review listed experimental bias as the main threat to the trial's validity.
examples.cn: 综述把实验偏差列为该试验效度的主要威胁。

examples.en: Random allocation was introduced to control experimental bias.
examples.cn: 引入随机分配是为了控制实验偏差。

examples.en: The team reported experimental bias from a change in the scoring rule.
examples.cn: 团队报告了评分规则改变带来的实验偏差。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「实验」加「斜」——实验者、受试者、分组、仪器，任何一方先歪一点，结果就跟着歪：实验偏差。

root: 拉丁 experimentum「试验」← experiri「尝试、考验」；古法语 biais「斜线」→ 英语 bias，更早来源不确定；统计方法赋予 bias「系统性偏离」的技术义，两者组合为实验偏差。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the people to the procedure: experimenter expectancy, participant response, assignment, confounding, measurement, order effects, analysis and reporting, and the remedies of blinding and randomisation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从人走向程序：实验者期望、受试者应答、分组、混杂、测量、顺序效应、分析与报告，以及盲法与随机化对策。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a researcher draws an expected arrow on the record sheet, and the participant walking past the group sign answers toward that arrow.
core.cn: 核心意象：研究者在记录表上画出预期箭头，受试者经过分组牌时，回答就朝那个箭头靠。

branches.en: THE TWO PEOPLE: the experimenter's expectation and the participant's reading of the study.
branches.cn: 两个人：实验者的期望与受试者对研究的理解。

branches.en: THE GROUPS AND THE SECOND CAUSE: unequal assignment and a confound travelling with the treatment.
branches.cn: 分组与第二原因：分组不均，以及随处理同行的混杂。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT: a tool that leans to one side.
branches.cn: 仪器：向一侧偏的工具。

branches.en: THE ORDER: learning, fatigue and carry-over between conditions.
branches.cn: 顺序：条件之间的学习、疲劳与残留。

branches.en: THE CHOICE AND THE GUARD: selecting favourable results, and blinding or randomising to prevent it.
branches.cn: 选择与防护：挑选有利结果，以及用盲法或随机化防止它。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin-derived noun for a trial to a French-derived noun for a slant.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁来源的「试验」名词与法语来源的「斜线」名词组合起来。

latinIntro.en: Latin experimentum supplies experiment; Old French biais supplies bias; the adjective ending -al and the compound are English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 experimentum 提供前半，古法语 biais 提供后半，形容词词尾与复合构词属英语。

items.example: It supplies the trial at the centre of the term.
items.exampleCN: 它提供术语中心的「试验」。

items.example: English took the noun as experiment.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个名词借为 experiment。

items.example: It forms experimental.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 experimental。

items.example: The -er ending names the first source of bias.
items.exampleCN: 施动者词尾命名第一个偏差来源。

items.example: The physical slope becomes a statistical one.
items.exampleCN: 物理斜面变成统计斜线。

items.example: The second half names the distortion.
items.exampleCN: 后半命名失真。

items.example: The -ed ending marks the affected state.
items.exampleCN: 已然词尾标出受影响的状态。

items.example: It forms unbiased, the desired state.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 unbiased，即所希望的状态。

items.example: The compound names the standard remedy.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词命名标准对策。

items.meaning: distortion from the conduct of a trial
items.meaningCN: 由试验实施造成的失真
items.example: The compound is a modern methodological label.

definition_zh: 客观性；客观态度；客观判断
definition_en: the quality of basing claims on evidence that does not depend on a particular person's feelings, interests or wishes
core_image: 天平两端放相同砝码，指针停在正中，旁边摊着一份任何人都能复核的记录
scene: 评审桌上摆着一架天平，两边砝码相同，指针停在正中，旁边摊着谁都能查的记录。Objectivity in science means that another team can reach the same result from the same records.
sceneCN: 这里指判断依据可公开复核的证据而不受个人偏好左右（第 1 个义项：判断的客观公正）；句意为科学中的客观性意味着另一支团队凭同样的记录能得出同样的结果。图中可辨识物件：天平、砝码、指针、记录册、评审桌。

pos.zh: 客观性；客观态度；客观判断

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 objectum 经法语而来，义为「对象；反对」
由该名词加形容词词尾构成，义为「客观的；目标」
由客观形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「客观地」
由该名词加表示「使成为」的动词词尾构成，义为「使客观化；物化」
由客观形容词加表示「主义」的词尾构成，义为「客观主义」

senses.title: Impartial judgment based on evidence
senses.definition: the quality of judging by evidence that others can inspect rather than by personal preference
senses.definitionCN: 以他人可核查的证据而非个人偏好来作判断的品质
senses.example: Objectivity in science means that another team can reach the same result from the same records.
senses.exampleCN: 科学中的客观性意味着另一支团队凭同样的记录能得出同样的结果。
senses.why: A judgment is objective when the reasons for it can be shown to someone who does not share the judge's interests.
senses.whyCN: 当判断的理由能展示给一个与判断者利益无关的人时，这个判断才是客观的。

senses.title: Independence from the researcher's bias
senses.definition: the discipline of keeping one's hypotheses, preferences and career interests from deciding what the data are allowed to say
senses.definitionCN: 不让自己的假设、偏好与职业利益决定数据能说什么的自我约束
senses.example: Objectivity does not require the researcher to have no hypothesis, only to test it fairly.
senses.exampleCN: 客观性并不要求研究者没有假设，只要求公平地检验它。
senses.why: The researcher cannot delete expectation, but can arrange the procedure so expectation has no route into the result.
senses.whyCN: 研究者无法删除期待，却可以安排程序，使期待没有路径进入结果。

senses.title: A reality independent of perception
senses.definition: the philosophical claim that objects and facts exist whether or not anyone observes or believes them
senses.definitionCN: 哲学主张：对象与事实是否存在，不取决于是否有人观察或相信
senses.example: The objectivity of the external world is a philosophical claim, not a laboratory finding.
senses.exampleCN: 外部世界的客观性是一个哲学主张，不是实验室的发现。
senses.why: The word begins with something thrown before the mind, and this sense asks whether that thing remains when the mind turns away.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「被抛到心灵之前的东西」开始，这个义项追问心灵转开之后那件东西是否还在。

senses.title: Objective measurement and protocol
senses.definition: the use of defined instruments, fixed procedures and explicit rules so that results do not depend on who happens to run the session
senses.definitionCN: 使用有定义的仪器、固定程序与明确规则，使结果不取决于谁碰巧执行
senses.example: Objective measurement requires that the zero point and the unit be stated in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 客观测量要求零点与单位预先写明。
senses.why: A measurement is objective when the procedure, not the mood of the measurer, fixes the number.
senses.whyCN: 当固定数字的是程序而非测量者的心情时，测量才是客观的。

senses.title: Objectivity in reporting
senses.titleCN: 报道与陈述中的客观性
senses.definition: the separation of verifiable fact from comment, and the attribution of claims to their sources
senses.definitionCN: 把可核实的事实与评论分开，并把说法归到相应来源
senses.example: The editor asked for objectivity in reporting, with every claim attributed.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑要求报道保持客观，每一条说法都要注明来源。
senses.why: A reader who cannot tell fact from comment cannot check either, so the separation is part of public trust.
senses.whyCN: 读者若分不清事实与评论，两者都无法核查，因此这种分离是公共信任的一部分。

senses.title: Fairness in assessment
senses.definition: the application of the same criteria to every case, with reasons that can be stated and reviewed
senses.definitionCN: 对每个个案适用同样标准，并给出可陈述、可复核的理由
senses.example: Objectivity in grading means that two markers reach the same score from the same script.
senses.exampleCN: 评分中的客观性意味着两位评阅人凭同一份答卷给出同样的分数。
senses.why: A grade that cannot be explained by its criteria is a personal verdict wearing the clothes of a measurement.
senses.whyCN: 无法按标准解释的分数，是披着测量外衣的个人裁决。

senses.title: The objectivity of a method
senses.definition: the extent to which a procedure yields the same result across observers, occasions and repetitions
senses.definitionCN: 一种程序在不同观察者、不同场合与重复执行下给出相同结果的程度
senses.example: Inter-rater agreement is one practical test of the objectivity of a coding scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 评分者一致性是检验编码方案客观性的一种实际办法。
senses.why: When a method is objective, the result travels without carrying the name of the person who produced it.
senses.whyCN: 当方法客观时，结果传播时不带着制作者的名字。

senses.title: The critique and the limit
senses.titleCN: 对客观性的批评与限度
senses.definition: the argument that no observer stands outside a perspective, so objectivity must be a discipline of checking rather than a view from nowhere
senses.definitionCN: 主张没有观察者能站在视角之外，因此客观性应是一种核查纪律，而不是「无处之见」
senses.example: The strongest defence of objectivity is procedural: disclose the perspective and invite challenge.
senses.exampleCN: 对客观性最有力的辩护是程序性的：公开视角并接受质疑。
senses.why: If a pure view from nowhere is impossible, objectivity survives as a set of habits that limit the damage of perspective.
senses.whyCN: 如果纯粹的无处之见不可能，客观性就作为一套限制视角损害的习惯而存在。

intro.en: Objectivity comes from Latin objectum, something thrown before the mind, from obicere, to throw against. The abstract noun is modern, built on objective.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 objectum「被抛到心灵之前的东西」，源出 obicere「抛向对面」；抽象名词是近代在 objective 基础上构成的。

items.en: Obicere meant to throw against or place before, from ob- against and iacere to throw.
items.cn: obicere 意为抛向对面或置于面前，由 ob-「对着」与 iacere「抛」构成。

items.en: Objectum named what is placed before the mind, the object of thought rather than the thinker.
items.cn: objectum 指被置于心灵之前的东西，是思想的对象而非思考者。

items.en: Scholastic Latin used objective for what exists in the mind as an object of thought, almost the reverse of the modern sense.
items.cn: 经院拉丁语用 objective 指以思想对象的方式存在，几乎与现代义相反。

items.en: Early modern philosophy reversed the emphasis, and objective came to mean belonging to the object rather than to the mind.
items.cn: 近代早期哲学颠倒重点，objective 转而指属于客体而非心灵。

items.en: The abstract noun objectivity spread in the nineteenth century with science and journalism; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 抽象名词 objectivity 在十九世纪随科学与新闻业传播；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Later thinkers argued that no observer escapes a perspective, which turned objectivity into a discipline of disclosure and checking.
items.cn: 后来的思想家主张没有观察者能摆脱视角，这使客观性变成一种公开与核查的纪律。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like objectivity; the second group names neighbouring ideas of fairness and evidence.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 objectivity 相近；第二组是与「公正、证据」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: A thing placed before the mind or before the senses.
entries.definitionCN: 指置于心灵或感官之前的事物。

entries.definition: Belonging to the object rather than to personal feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 指属于客体而非个人感受的。

entries.definition: In a way that can be checked by others.
entries.definitionCN: 指以他人可核查的方式。

entries.definition: To treat something as an object, often with a critical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物当作客体，常带批评意味。

entries.definition: A statement thrown against a claim; it shares the Latin verb but not the sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指针对某主张提出的反对；共享拉丁动词但词义不同。

entries.definition: Freedom from favouring one side over another.
entries.definitionCN: 指不偏袒任何一方。

entries.definition: Taking no side in a dispute.
entries.definitionCN: 指在争端中不选边。

entries.definition: Treating cases by the same standard.
entries.definitionCN: 指以同一标准对待各个个案。

entries.definition: Consistency of a measure across occasions or raters.
entries.definitionCN: 指测量在不同场合或评分者之间的一致程度。

entries.definition: Emotional distance from the object of study.
entries.definitionCN: 指与研究对象的情绪距离。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations work through the real parts, word family and common phrases behind this term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想依托这个术语背后真实的构词部件、同族词与常见搭配。

normal.en: Objectum is something thrown before the mind, so objectivity begins with an object rather than a feeling.
normal.cn: objectum 是被抛到心灵之前的东西，因此客观性从客体而非感受开始。

normal.en: Objective and subjectivity are a pair, but they are not two rooms with a wall between; each needs the other to be defined.
normal.cn: 客观性与主观性是一对，但不是隔墙两间房；各自都需要对方才能被定义。

normal.en: A zero point and a unit are the grammar of objective measurement.
normal.cn: 零点与单位是客观测量的语法。

normal.en: Two markers reaching the same score is objectivity made visible.
normal.cn: 两位评阅人给出同一分数，是客观性变得可见。

normal.en: Attribution turns a claim into something a reader can trace.
normal.cn: 注明来源使一个说法变成读者可以追溯的东西。

abstract.en: Objectivity is not the absence of a perspective but the willingness to let the perspective be inspected.
abstract.cn: 客观性不是没有视角，而是愿意让视角接受检查。

abstract.en: The view from nowhere is a useful ideal precisely because no one can stand there.
abstract.cn: 「无处之见」是有用的理想，正因无人能站在那里。

abstract.en: A mirror is objective only until someone forgets to clean it; so is a method.
abstract.cn: 镜子只有在没人忘记擦的时候才客观；方法也是如此。

examples.en: The panel questioned the objectivity of a report funded by the industry it studied.
examples.cn: 评审组质疑一份由被研究行业资助的报告的客观性。

examples.en: Objectivity improves when the raw records are published alongside the conclusion.
examples.cn: 当原始记录与结论一同公布时，客观性会提高。

examples.en: She treated objectivity as a practice of checking, not as a claim of having no perspective.
examples.cn: 她把客观性当作一种核查实践，而不是宣称自己没有视角。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「客体」加「性」——把东西放在天平上，两边砝码一样，谁来看都读同一个数：客观性。

root: 拉丁 obicere「抛向对面」← ob-「对着」+ iacere「抛」，名词 objectum「被置于心灵之前的东西」；近代哲学把重点从心灵转向客体，十九世纪形成抽象名词 objectivity。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from judgment to critique: impartial judgment, independence from researcher bias, an external reality, objective measurement, reporting, fair assessment, the objectivity of methods, and the critique of the ideal itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从判断走向反思：公正判断、不受研究者偏差影响、外部实在、客观测量、报道、公平评价、方法客观性，以及对这一理想本身的批评。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance with equal weights, its pointer resting at the centre, beside a record that anyone may inspect.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架两端砝码相同的天平，指针停在正中，旁边摊着谁都能查的记录。

branches.en: THE FAIR JUDGMENT: the same standard applied to every case, with reasons that can be stated.
branches.cn: 公正判断：对每个个案适用同一标准，并给出可陈述的理由。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE OF THE RESEARCHER: expectation kept out of the route to the result.
branches.cn: 研究者的纪律：不让期待进入结果的通路。

branches.en: THE INDEPENDENT WORLD: facts that remain when the observer turns away.
branches.cn: 独立世界：观察者转开之后仍然存在的事实。

branches.en: THE PROCEDURE AND THE METHOD: fixed instruments, and agreement across observers.
branches.cn: 程序与方法：固定的仪器，以及观察者之间的一致。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC AND THE LIMIT: attributed reporting, and the recognition that no view is from nowhere.
branches.cn: 公开与限度：注明来源的报道，以及承认没有无处之见。

intro.en: Objectivity is a Latin-derived abstract noun built on objective, which descends from objectum.
intro.cn: 这是一个拉丁来源的抽象名词，建立在「客观的」这一形容词之上，而该形容词又出自 objectum。

latinIntro.en: Latin iacere and obicere supply the throwing before the mind; objectum supplies the noun; -ive and -ity are English endings that turn it into a quality.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 iacere 与 obicere 提供「抛到心灵之前」的动作，objectum 提供名词，形容词词尾与名词词尾把它变成一种性质。

definition_zh: 主观性；主体性；主观感受
definition_en: the quality of belonging to a particular person's experience, perspective or judgment rather than to an independent external fact
core_image: 同一幅画前两位观者各写一页感受，一个说暖，一个说冷，画框始终不动

sceneCN: 这里指个人感受与视角的介入（第 1 个义项：属于个人经验的主观性）；句意为当两位读者用相反的方式描述同一页时，主观性就进来了。图中可辨识物件：画框、两页笔记、两支笔、观者、同一幅画。

pos.zh: 主观性；主体性；主观感受

由该名词加形容词词尾构成，义为「主观的」
