senses.title: A particular person's experience
senses.definition: the quality of an experience as it is lived from one person's point of view and not as it is measured from outside
senses.definitionCN: 经验从某一个人的角度被经历、而非从外部被测量的性质
senses.example: Subjectivity enters when two readers describe the same page in opposite ways.
senses.exampleCN: 当两位读者用相反的方式描述同一页时，主观性就进来了。
senses.why: Two people can face the same object and carry away different experiences, because experience is lived from inside a life.
senses.whyCN: 两个人面对同一物体，却带走不同的经验，因为经验是从某一段人生内部被经历的。

senses.title: A judgment shaped by personal preference
senses.titleCN: 受个人偏好影响的判断
senses.definition: a judgment in which taste, memory or interest plays a part that the judge may not fully see
senses.definitionCN: 品味、记忆或利益参与其中而判断者未必完全察觉的判断
senses.example: The choice of colour is subjective, while the size of the frame is not.
senses.exampleCN: 颜色的选择是主观的，而画框的尺寸不是。
senses.why: Preference is not a defect in every judgment; it becomes a problem only when it is presented as independent fact.
senses.whyCN: 偏好并非在所有判断里都是缺陷；只有当它被当作独立事实呈现时，才成为问题。

senses.title: The researcher's own presence in qualitative work
senses.titleCN: 定性研究中研究者自身的在场
senses.definition: the part played by the researcher's background, relationship and reactions in shaping what is noticed and asked
senses.definitionCN: 研究者的背景、关系与反应在决定注意什么、追问什么时所起的作用
senses.example: Qualitative work treats subjectivity as data to be documented rather than as noise to be removed.
senses.exampleCN: 定性工作把主观性当作需要记录的数据，而不是需要清除的噪声。
senses.why: The interviewer is one of the instruments, so the instrument's position must be described.
senses.whyCN: 访谈者本身就是工具之一，因此这件工具的位置必须被描述。

senses.title: Emotional and affective life
senses.definition: the felt side of experience, including mood, emotion and bodily sensation
senses.definitionCN: 经验中被感受到的一面，包括心情、情绪与身体感觉
senses.example: Pain is known through subjectivity as well as through a scale from one to ten.
senses.exampleCN: 疼痛既通过主观感受被认识，也通过一到十的评分被认识。
senses.why: A number can record the intensity of pain, but only the person can report what the pain is like.
senses.whyCN: 数字可以记录疼痛的强度，但只有本人能报告疼痛是什么感觉。

senses.title: The philosophical subject
senses.definition: the conscious self that experiences, thinks and acts, considered as the bearer of experience
senses.definitionCN: 作为经验、思考与行动承担者的有意识自我
senses.example: Philosophy asks how a subject can know anything beyond its own subjectivity.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学追问主体如何能认识自身主观性之外的东西。
senses.why: This sense is about the bearer of experience rather than about a person's opinions.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项讲的是经验的承担者，而不是某人的意见。

senses.title: The subjectivity of perception
senses.definition: the ways in which the senses select, organise and colour what is present
senses.definitionCN: 感官对在场之物进行选择、组织与着色
senses.example: Colour constancy is a reminder that perception has its own subjectivity.
senses.exampleCN: 颜色恒常性提醒我们，感知有自己的主观性。
senses.why: The eye is not a window but an organ with habits, and those habits enter every observation.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛不是窗户，而是有习惯的器官，而这些习惯进入每一次观察。

senses.title: The interpretive lens in analysis
senses.definition: the frame of meaning a person brings to reading a text, an action or a dataset
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在阅读文本、行为或数据集时带入的意义框架
senses.example: Two coders agreed on the words but differed in the subjectivity of their reading.
senses.exampleCN: 两位编码员对字面一致，却在解读的主观性上不同。
senses.why: Meaning is not stored in the text like an object in a box; it is assembled by a reader with a history.
senses.whyCN: 意义不像箱子里的物品那样存放在文本中，而是由带着历史的读者组装起来。

senses.title: Subjectivity and objectivity together
senses.titleCN: 主观性与客观性的关系
senses.definition: the relation in which subjective position is disclosed so that objective checking remains possible
senses.definitionCN: 公开主观位置从而使客观核查仍然可能的关系
senses.example: Subjectivity is not the opposite of rigor when it is named and examined.
senses.exampleCN: 当主观性被命名并接受检视时，它就不是严谨的对立面。
senses.why: The pair works like a scale and a hand: the hand must be visible for the reading to be trusted.
senses.whyCN: 这一对像秤与手：手必须看得见，读数才可信。

intro.en: Subjectivity comes from Latin subjectum, something placed under, from subicere, to place beneath. The abstract noun is modern.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 subjectum「被置于下方的东西」，源出 subicere「置于下面」；抽象名词是近代构成的。

items.en: Subicere meant to place under or subject, from sub- under and iacere to throw.
items.cn: subicere 意为置于下方或使服从，由 sub-「在下」与 iacere「抛」构成。

items.en: Subjectum named what lies beneath, whether a substance, a topic or a person under authority.
items.cn: subjectum 指位于下方的东西，无论是实体、主题还是受支配的人。

items.en: Medieval philosophy used subject for the bearer of qualities, and the word became the opposite of object.
items.cn: 中世纪哲学用 subject 指性质的承担者，这个词后来成为 object 的对立面。

items.en: Descartes and later thinkers made the subject the conscious self that thinks and experiences.
items.cn: 笛卡尔及后来的思想家把 subject 变成思考与经验的有意识自我。

items.en: The abstract noun appeared with modern philosophy and psychology; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 抽象名词随近代哲学与心理学出现；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Social research later adopted subjectivity as a named feature of the researcher's position rather than a simple error.
items.cn: 社会科学后来把主观性当作研究者位置的一种明确特征，而不是简单的错误。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like subjectivity; the second group names neighbouring ideas of personal position and interpretation.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 subjectivity 相近；第二组是与「个人位置、解释」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: A topic, a person under authority, or the conscious self.
entries.definitionCN: 指主题、受支配的人或有意识的自我。

entries.definition: Belonging to personal experience or judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 指属于个人经验或判断的。

entries.definition: From the point of view of the person concerned.
entries.definitionCN: 指从当事人角度出发。

entries.definition: The state of being placed under control.
entries.definitionCN: 指被置于控制之下的状态。

entries.definition: A verb mood; it comes from a different Latin verb meaning to join under.
entries.definitionCN: 指一种动词语气；来自另一个意为「接在下面」的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: A particular standpoint from which something is seen.
entries.definitionCN: 指观看某物的特定立足点。

entries.definition: The researcher's social location and its effect on the work.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究者的社会位置及其对研究的影响。

entries.definition: The meaning a reader or analyst draws from material.
entries.definitionCN: 指读者或分析者从材料中得出的意义。

entries.definition: A felt state such as fear, joy or grief.
entries.definitionCN: 指恐惧、喜悦或悲伤等被感受到的状态。

entries.definition: A systematic slant that distorts a judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 指使判断失真的系统性倾向。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations work through the real parts, word family and common phrases behind this term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想依托这个术语背后真实的构词部件、同族词与常见搭配。

normal.en: Subjectum lies under, and objectivity throws something before; the two words face each other across the mind.
normal.cn: subjectum 位于下方，「客观性」却把某物抛到前方；两个词隔着一颗心灵相对。

normal.en: Subjectivity is not the same as bias: bias is a slant that can be corrected, subjectivity is a position that must be disclosed.
normal.cn: 主观性不等于偏差：偏差是可以纠正的斜线，主观性是必须公开的位置。

normal.en: Qualitative researchers write reflexive notes because their own presence is part of the instrument.
normal.cn: 定性研究者写反思笔记，因为他们自身的在场是工具的一部分。

normal.en: Pain has a number and a feeling, and the two are not substitutes.
normal.cn: 疼痛有一个数字，也有一种感觉，二者不能互相替代。

normal.en: Two coders can agree on every word and still read the passage differently.
normal.cn: 两位编码员可以对每个字都一致，却仍对段落有不同解读。

abstract.en: A perspective is not a prison unless it is presented as a window with no frame.
abstract.cn: 视角本身不是牢房，除非它被呈现为一扇没有边框的窗。

abstract.en: The reader brings the furniture of a lifetime into a room of three sentences.
abstract.cn: 读者把一生的家具搬进只有三句话的房间。

abstract.en: Subjectivity becomes trustworthy when it stops hiding and starts describing itself.
abstract.cn: 当主观性不再躲藏而开始描述自己时，它才变得可信。

examples.en: The paper describes researcher subjectivity as part of the evidence rather than as a defect.
examples.cn: 该论文把研究者的主观性描述为证据的一部分，而不是缺陷。

examples.en: Subjectivity of experience cannot be replaced by a laboratory reading.
examples.cn: 经验的主观性无法被实验室读数取代。

examples.en: Reflexive notes made the team's subjectivity visible to readers.
examples.cn: 反思笔记让团队的主观性对读者可见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「主体」加「性」——同一幅画，一人说暖、一人说冷；画不动，感受各自带着自己的位置：主观性。

root: 拉丁 subicere「置于下方」← sub-「在下」+ iacere「抛」，名词 subjectum「位于下方的东西」；中世纪指性质的承担者，近代哲学转为有意识的自我，十九世纪形成抽象名词 subjectivity。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from lived experience toward the analytic lens: personal experience, preference in judgment, the researcher's presence, emotional life, the philosophical subject, perception, interpretation, and the relation to objectivity.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从亲历经验走向分析视角：个人经验、判断中的偏好、研究者的在场、情绪生活、哲学主体、感知、解释，以及与客观性的关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two viewers stand before one unchanged painting and write opposite accounts of its warmth.
core.cn: 核心意象：两位观者站在同一幅未变的画前，写下相反的温度感受。

branches.en: THE LIVED INSIDE: experience and feeling as they are felt from within one life.
branches.cn: 亲历之内：从一段人生内部被经历的经验与感受。

branches.en: THE PREFERENCE: taste entering a judgment that may be presented as fact.
branches.cn: 偏好：品味进入一个可能被当作事实的判断。

branches.en: THE RESEARCHER'S LENS: presence in the field and the frame brought to interpretation.
branches.cn: 研究者的透镜：在现场的在场，以及带入解释的框架。

branches.en: THE SUBJECT AND THE SENSES: the conscious bearer, and perception with its own habits.
branches.cn: 主体与感官：有意识的承担者，以及带自身习惯的感知。

branches.en: THE PAIR WITH OBJECTIVITY: a named position that remains open to checking.
branches.cn: 与客观性成对：被命名的位置仍向核查开放。

intro.en: Subjectivity is a Latin-derived abstract noun built on subjective, which descends from subjectum.
intro.cn: 这是一个拉丁来源抽象名词，建立在「主观的」这一形容词之上，而该形容词又出自 subjectum。

latinIntro.en: Latin sub- and iacere supply the placing beneath; subjectum supplies the noun; -ive and -ity are English endings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sub- 与 iacere 提供「置于下方」的动作，subjectum 提供名词，形容词词尾与名词词尾完成抽象化。

items.exampleCN: 它把主体置于性质或权力之下。

items.example: The same verb lies behind object.
items.exampleCN: 同一个动词也藏在 object 背后。

items.structure: Latin verb from sub- plus iacere
items.example: The verb supplies the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供词族。

items.example: It becomes English subject.
items.exampleCN: 它成为英语 subject。

items.meaning: a topic, a person under rule, or the self
items.example: English keeps several layers at once.
items.exampleCN: 英语同时保留数层含义。

items.example: It forms subjective.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 subjective。

items.example: It forms subjectivity.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 subjectivity。

items.example: It forms subjectively.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 subjectively。

items.example: The paired word uses the same verb with the opposite prefix.
items.exampleCN: 配对词用同一动词但相反前缀。

items.example: The term names subjectivity made explicit.
items.exampleCN: 这个术语指被明确说出的主观性。

senses.title: A systematic reading of ambiguity
senses.titleCN: 对歧义信息的系统性解读偏向
senses.definition: a tendency to resolve ambiguous material in one consistent direction, such as reading it as threat rather than as neutral
senses.definitionCN: 倾向以某个固定方向消解歧义材料，例如总读成威胁而非中性
senses.example: Interpretation bias can turn the same ambiguous reply into reassurance or threat.
senses.exampleCN: 解释偏差可以把同一句含糊的回应读成安慰，也可以读成威胁。
senses.why: When a signal has more than one meaning, the reader must choose, and a habit of choosing makes the choice systematic.
senses.whyCN: 当一个信号有多种含义时，读者必须选择，而选择的习惯使这种选择变得系统。

senses.title: The researcher's interpretive bias
senses.definition: a researcher's tendency to notice, select and code material in line with an existing frame
senses.definitionCN: 研究者按既有框架去注意、挑选与编码材料的倾向
senses.example: Interpretation bias in coding appeared as a preference for quotations that supported the main theme.
senses.exampleCN: 编码中的解释偏差表现为偏好支持主主题的引语。
senses.why: The analyst is not a neutral reader; the coding scheme and the expected finding both steer attention.
senses.whyCN: 分析者不是中性读者；编码方案与预期发现都会引导注意力。

senses.title: Confirmation-driven reading
senses.definition: the tendency to treat consistent evidence as strong and inconsistent evidence as flawed
senses.definitionCN: 把一致证据视为有力、把不一致证据视为有缺陷的倾向
senses.example: Interpretation bias made the team dismiss the two cases that contradicted the pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 解释偏差使团队忽略了两个与模式相矛盾的个案。
senses.why: A hypothesis is comfortable with friends and suspicious of strangers, and the reader inherits that comfort.
senses.whyCN: 假设对朋友感到舒服、对陌生人心存怀疑，而读者继承了这种舒服。

senses.title: A cultural or linguistic lens
senses.definition: the way a shared language, custom or educational tradition supplies a default meaning for a word or act
senses.definitionCN: 共同语言、习俗或教育传统为一个词或行为提供默认含义的方式
senses.example: Interpretation bias across languages can turn a polite refusal into agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 跨语言解释偏差可以把礼貌的拒绝读成同意。
senses.why: A word translated word for word may arrive with a meaning it never had in the original setting.
senses.whyCN: 逐字翻译过来的词，可能带着它在原场景中从未有过的含义到达。

senses.title: Bias built into a coding category
senses.titleCN: 编码类别本身带来的偏向
senses.definition: distortion produced when predefined categories force complex material into one available box
senses.definitionCN: 预设类别把复杂材料塞进现有格子而产生的失真
senses.example: A narrow coding frame creates interpretation bias before the first transcript is read.
senses.exampleCN: 狭窄的编码框架在第一份逐字稿被读之前就造成了偏差。
senses.why: A category is a question the data must answer, and some answers have no category to enter.
senses.whyCN: 类别是数据必须回答的问题，而有些回答根本没有类别可进。

senses.title: Bias in attributing causes
senses.definition: a tendency to explain an act by the actor's character in one group and by the situation in another
senses.definitionCN: 倾向把某一群体的行为解释为性格，而把另一群体的行为解释为情境
senses.example: Interpretation bias appeared in the way the same delay was blamed on laziness or on traffic.
senses.exampleCN: 同样的延误，一个被归为懒惰，一个被归为堵车，解释偏差就在这里出现。
senses.why: The same event admits a dispositional and a situational reading, and the choice between them can follow a group line.
senses.whyCN: 同一件事既可以按性格解释，也可以按情境解释，而选择往往沿着群体界线走。

senses.title: The effect on trustworthiness
senses.definition: the loss of credibility when readers cannot tell whether a finding comes from the data or from the analyst's frame
senses.definitionCN: 读者无法判断发现来自数据还是分析者框架时所造成的可信度损失
senses.example: Interpretation bias weakens trustworthiness even when the interviews were well conducted.
senses.exampleCN: 即使访谈做得很好，解释偏差也会削弱可信度。
senses.why: If the frame is invisible, the finding looks like the data speaking in its own voice, which is the problem.
senses.whyCN: 如果框架不可见，发现就像数据用自己的声音说话，问题正在这里。

senses.title: Reflexivity and peer coding as remedies
senses.titleCN: 反思与同伴编码作为对策
senses.definition: the practices of recording one's interpretive frame and having a second coder check the reading
senses.definitionCN: 记录自身解释框架并让第二位编码员核查解读的做法
senses.example: Peer coding is used to make interpretation bias visible rather than to pretend it is absent.
senses.exampleCN: 同伴编码用来让解释偏差变得可见，而不是假装它不存在。
senses.why: A second reader does not remove the lens, but can show where the lens is bending the material.
senses.whyCN: 第二位读者无法取下透镜，却能指出透镜在哪里弯折了材料。

intro.en: Interpretation bias joins interpretari, a Latin verb of explaining, to bias, from Old French biais, a slant. The origin of interpres, the Latin noun behind the verb, is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个术语把拉丁语解释动词 interpretari 与来自古法语 biais「斜线」的 bias 组合起来；动词背后的名词 interpres 来源不确定。

items.en: Interpres meant a go-between, explainer or negotiator, but its own origin is source uncertain; a link to a word for price has been proposed.
items.cn: interpres 指中间人、解释者或谈判者，但它自身的来源不确定；有人提出与表示「价格」的词有关。

items.en: Interpretari meant to explain, expound or translate, and it supplied the English verb.
items.cn: interpretari 意为解释、阐发或翻译，提供英语动词 interpret。

items.en: English used interpret for explaining meaning and for oral translation; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语用 interpret 表示解释意义与口译；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The noun named an explanation or a translation, and English took it as interpretation.
items.cn: 名词指解释或翻译，英语借入为 interpretation。

items.en: Biais meant a slant or an oblique line, and its deeper origin is also uncertain.
items.cn: biais 意为斜面或斜线，其更早来源同样不确定。

items.en: Psychology and qualitative methods joined the two nouns to name a systematic reading habit, whether in a person or in an analyst.
items.cn: 心理学与定性方法把这两个名词组合，指一种系统的解读习惯，无论在个人还是在分析者身上。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like interpretation bias; the second group names neighbouring distortions of reading and analysis.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 interpretation bias 相近；第二组是与「阅读与分析失真」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: To explain or assign meaning to material.
entries.definitionCN: 指解释或为材料赋予意义。

entries.definition: The meaning drawn from material, or the act of drawing it.
entries.definitionCN: 指从材料中得出的意义，或得出意义的行为。

entries.definition: A person who explains or translates speech.
entries.definitionCN: 指解释或口译的人。

entries.definition: Relating to explanation rather than measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 指与解释而非测量有关的。

entries.definition: To read something in a wrong way.
entries.definitionCN: 指以错误方式解读某物。

entries.definition: The tendency to seek and accept evidence that supports an existing belief.
entries.definitionCN: 指寻求并接受支持既有信念的证据的倾向。

entries.definition: Distortion introduced by the categories and rules used to label material.
entries.definitionCN: 指由标记材料的类别与规则引入的失真。

entries.definition: A systematic error in explaining the causes of behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 指解释行为原因时的系统性错误。

entries.definition: The way a question or frame makes some meanings more available.
entries.definitionCN: 指问题或框架使某些意义更易得的方式。

entries.definition: The practice of examining one's own position in the research.
entries.definitionCN: 指检视自身在研究中所处位置的做法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations work through the real parts, word family and common phrases behind this term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想依托这个术语背后真实的构词部件、同族词与常见搭配。

normal.en: Interpres was a go-between, and an interpreter stands between two parties who do not share a language.
normal.cn: interpres 是中间人，解释者站在两个语言不通的人之间。

normal.en: The same sentence can be read as threat or reassurance, and the habit of reading decides.
normal.cn: 同一句话可以读成威胁，也可以读成安慰，而阅读习惯作决定。

normal.en: A coding frame is a set of boxes, and material that fits no box is the first thing lost.
normal.cn: 编码框架是一组格子，放不进格子的材料最先丢失。

normal.en: Confirmation bias makes friends of consistent evidence and strangers of the rest.
normal.cn: 确认偏差把一致证据当朋友，把其余当陌生人。

normal.en: Peer coding does not remove the lens; it makes the lens visible.
normal.cn: 同伴编码不取下透镜，而是让透镜可见。

abstract.en: A text does not carry its meaning the way a box carries a stone; someone has to lift it.
abstract.cn: 文本携带意义不像箱子装石头，必须有人把它搬起来。

abstract.en: The frame you cannot see is the one that looks like the world.
abstract.cn: 你看不见的那个框架，最像世界本身。

abstract.en: Two readers can agree on every word and still live in different sentences.
abstract.cn: 两位读者可以对每个字都一致，却仍住在不同的句子里。

examples.en: The authors named interpretation bias as a limit of single-coder analysis.
examples.cn: 作者把解释偏差列为单人编码分析的一种局限。

examples.en: Training reduced interpretation bias in the scoring of open-ended answers.
examples.cn: 培训减少了开放式答案评分中的解释偏差。

examples.en: A second coder was added to expose interpretation bias in the theme labels.
examples.cn: 加入第二位编码员，以暴露主题标签中的解释偏差。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「解释」加「斜」——同一句话，有人读出安慰，有人读出威胁；斜的那一下，就是解释偏差。

root: 拉丁 interpres「中间人、解释者」（来源不确定，可能与「价格」有关）+ interpretari「解释、翻译」→ 英语 interpret / interpretation；古法语 biais「斜线」→ bias（更早来源不确定）；两者组合为解释偏差。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the ambiguous signal to the remedy: systematic reading of ambiguity, the researcher's frame, confirmation-driven reading, cultural lenses, category bias, attribution bias, effects on trustworthiness, and reflexivity or peer coding.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从歧义信号走向补救：对歧义的系统解读、研究者框架、确认驱动、文化透镜、类别偏差、归因偏差、对可信度的影响，以及反思与同伴编码。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one transcript on a table, two highlighters marking different sentences, and two coding sheets in different colours.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上一份访谈稿，两支荧光笔划出不同句子，两份编码表用不同颜色标记。

definition_en: the condition in which the probability of obtaining an observed result, assuming a stated null hypothesis, falls below a threshold fixed in advance
core_image: 一条分布曲线，尾部一小块被涂红，竖线把红区与主体分开，旁边放着阈值卡片

sceneCN: 这里指统计检验中的显著性（第 1 个义项：结果在既定阈值下不太可能由随机产生）；句意为统计显著性回答的是这个模式是否很容易由偶然产生。图中可辨识物件：分布曲线、红色尾区、竖线阈值、评审人、打印纸。

由拉丁语 significare「示意」而来，义为「表示；意味着」

senses.title: A result beyond a stated threshold
senses.definition: a result whose probability under the null hypothesis is lower than a threshold chosen before the test
senses.definitionCN: 在零假设下出现的概率低于事前选定阈值的结果
senses.example: Statistical significance answers whether the pattern could easily have appeared by chance.
senses.exampleCN: 统计显著性回答的是这个模式是否很容易由偶然产生。
senses.why: The threshold turns a continuous probability into a decision, which is why the word sounds like a yes or no.
senses.whyCN: 阈值把一个连续的概率变成一项决定，因此这个词听起来像「是」或「否」。

senses.title: Importance in the everyday sense
senses.definition: the quality of being important, meaningful or worth attention, with no reference to probability
senses.definitionCN: 重要、有意义或值得注意的性质，与概率无关
senses.example: The significance of the finding for patients is not the same as its statistical significance.
senses.exampleCN: 这一发现对患者的重要性，与其统计显著性并不是一回事。
senses.why: The word had this sense long before statistics borrowed it, and the older sense still lives in ordinary speech.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在统计学借用之前早就有这个义项，旧义至今活在日常语言里。

senses.title: A decision in a hypothesis test
senses.definition: the outcome of comparing a test statistic with a critical value or a probability with a threshold
senses.definitionCN: 把检验统计量与临界值比较、或把概率与阈值比较所得的结果
senses.example: The team reported statistical significance after comparing the two groups.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在比较两组之后报告了统计显著性。
senses.why: A test reduces a model and a dataset to one number, and that number is then read against a line.
senses.whyCN: 检验把模型与数据压缩成一个数，再把这个数对着一条线来读。

senses.title: The threshold and the critical region
senses.definition: the pre-set probability or critical value that separates a significant from a non-significant result
senses.definitionCN: 预先设定、用来区分显著与不显著结果的概率或临界值
senses.example: Changing the threshold changes what counts as statistical significance.
senses.exampleCN: 改变阈值就改变了什么算作统计显著性。
senses.why: The line is a human decision, and moving it moves the border between the two verdicts.
senses.whyCN: 这条线是人的决定，移动它也就移动了两种结论之间的边界。

senses.title: Practical significance and effect size
senses.definition: the size of an effect in the real world, which can be small even when the probability is below the threshold
senses.definitionCN: 效应在现实世界中的大小，即使概率低于阈值也可能很小
senses.example: Statistical significance does not guarantee practical significance in a large sample.
senses.exampleCN: 在大样本中，统计显著性并不保证实际意义。
senses.why: A large sample makes tiny differences detectable, so detectability and importance separate.
senses.whyCN: 大样本能让极小的差异被检出，于是「能检出」与「重要」分开了。

senses.title: The multiple-testing problem
senses.definition: inflation of false positives when many tests are run and only the significant ones are reported
senses.definitionCN: 运行许多检验、只报告显著者时假阳性被放大的问题
senses.example: Repeated tests can produce statistical significance with no real pattern behind it.
senses.exampleCN: 反复检验可以在背后没有真实模式的情况下产生统计显著性。
senses.why: Each test has a small chance of a false alarm, and many tests multiply that chance.
senses.whyCN: 每次检验都有一点误报机会，许多次检验把这一点机会累加起来。

senses.title: Reporting and the language of stars
senses.definition: the convention of marking results with probability levels, stars or verbal labels in publications
senses.definitionCN: 在出版物中用概率水平、星号或文字标签标记结果的做法
senses.example: The table marks statistical significance with three levels of stars.
senses.exampleCN: 表格用三级星号标出统计显著性。
senses.why: A convention compresses a long calculation into one symbol, and the symbol then travels without the calculation.
senses.whyCN: 惯例把长计算压缩成一个符号，而符号传播时并不带着计算。

senses.title: Misreading and the reproducibility question
senses.definition: the error of treating a threshold result as proof of importance, truth or a large effect
senses.definitionCN: 把达到阈值的结果当作重要性、真实性或大效应的证明的错误
senses.example: Statistical significance is not proof that the hypothesis is true.
senses.exampleCN: 统计显著性并不是假设为真的证明。
senses.why: The threshold was designed to control one kind of error, not to certify a conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 阈值是为控制某一类错误而设，不是为结论颁发证书。

intro.en: Statistical significance joins statistics, a German-coined science named from Latin status, a state, to significance, from Latin significare, to make a sign.
intro.cn: 这个术语把 statistics（由德语按拉丁语 status「状态」造出的学科名）与 significance（来自拉丁语 significare「作出记号」）组合起来。

items.en: Status meant a standing or a condition, and the modern science of the state took its name from it.
items.cn: status 意为状态或处境，近代关于国家的学问从这里取名。

items.en: German Statistik named the systematic description of a state's population and resources.
items.cn: 德语 Statistik 指对国家人口与资源的系统描述。

items.en: English borrowed statistics in the eighteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入 statistics；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Signum meant a mark or a sign, and significare meant to make a sign or convey meaning.
items.cn: signum 意为记号，significare 意为作出记号或传达意义。

items.en: Significantia meant meaning or importance, the everyday sense that statistics later narrowed.
items.cn: significantia 意为意义或重要性，即统计学后来加以窄化的日常义。

items.en: Fisher and others fixed the threshold and the vocabulary, and statistical significance became a standard phrase; exact priority is debated.
items.cn: 费希尔等人确定了阈值与术语，统计显著性成为标准说法；具体首创归属仍有争议。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like statistical significance; the second group names neighbouring quantities in a hypothesis test.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 statistical significance 相近；第二组是与「假设检验量」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The science of collecting and analysing data.
entries.definitionCN: 指收集与分析数据的学问。

entries.definition: Relating to that science.
entries.definitionCN: 指与这门学问有关的。

entries.definition: Importance, or a probability below a threshold.
entries.definitionCN: 指重要性，或低于阈值的概率。

entries.definition: Important, or statistically beyond the threshold.
entries.definitionCN: 指重要的，或统计上超过阈值的。

entries.definition: To mean or to indicate.
entries.definitionCN: 指意味着或标示。

entries.definition: The magnitude of a difference, independent of sample size.
entries.definitionCN: 指差异的大小，与样本量无关。

entries.definition: The threshold probability fixed before a test.
entries.definitionCN: 指检验前固定的阈值概率。

entries.definition: The chance of a result at least as extreme under the null hypothesis.
entries.definitionCN: 指零假设下出现至少同样极端结果的概率。

entries.definition: A range of plausible values for a parameter.
entries.definitionCN: 指参数的一组可能取值区间。

entries.definition: A procedure that compares data with a null model.
entries.definitionCN: 指把数据与零模型比较的程序。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations work through the real parts, word family and common phrases behind this term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想依托这个术语背后真实的构词部件、同族词与常见搭配。

normal.en: Significance first meant importance, and statistics borrowed the word for a probability below a line.
normal.cn: 「显著性」最初指重要性，统计学借它表示低于某条线的概率。

normal.en: The threshold is chosen before the test, which is why moving it afterwards is a form of cheating.
normal.cn: 阈值在检验前选定，因此事后移动它形同作弊。

normal.en: A tiny effect can be significant in a huge sample, and a large effect can miss the line in a small one.
normal.cn: 巨大样本里极小的效应也可能显著，小样本里很大的效应也可能够不到那条线。

normal.en: Every additional test adds another chance of a false alarm.
normal.cn: 每多做一次检验，就多一次误报机会。

normal.en: Stars in a table are a compressed sentence about probability, not a certificate of truth.
normal.cn: 表格里的星号是一句关于概率的压缩话，不是真理证书。

abstract.en: A threshold is a door that can be moved, and the same result may be inside or outside depending on who moved it.
abstract.cn: 阈值是一扇可以移动的门，同一个结果是否在门内，取决于谁移动了门。

abstract.en: Significance answers a question about chance, while importance answers a question about consequences.
abstract.cn: 显著性回答关于偶然的问题，重要性回答关于后果的问题。

abstract.en: A result becomes a fact by leaving the table, and the word significant is often the passport.
abstract.cn: 结果离开表格后成为事实，而「显著的」一词常是那本护照。

examples.en: The authors reported statistical significance but warned that the effect was small.
examples.cn: 作者报告了统计显著性，同时提醒效应很小。

examples.en: Statistical significance depends on the sample size as well as on the size of the difference.
examples.cn: 统计显著性既取决于差异大小，也取决于样本量。

examples.en: The review questioned how statistical significance had been used in the trial reports.
examples.cn: 该综述质疑统计显著性在试验报告中的使用方式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「统计」加「显著」——曲线尾巴被涂红，竖线一划，结果过了线就叫显著；过了线不等于重要。

root: 拉丁 status「状态」→ 德语 Statistik → 英语 statistics；拉丁 signum「记号」+ facere「做」→ significare「传达意义」→ significantia「意义、重要性」；二十世纪统计学把 significance 窄化为「低于阈值的概率」，与 statistical 组合成术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the threshold result to its misuse: a result beyond a threshold, everyday importance, a test decision, the critical region, effect size, multiple testing, reporting conventions, and misreading.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从阈值结果走向误用：超出阈值的结果、日常重要性、检验决定、拒绝域、效应量、多重检验、报告惯例，以及误读。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a distribution curve with one red tail, a vertical line cutting it off, and a threshold card beside the printout.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条分布曲线，一侧尾巴被涂红，一条竖线把它切下，打印纸旁放着阈值卡片。

branches.en: THE THRESHOLD RESULT: a probability below the pre-set line, and the critical region that defines it.
branches.cn: 阈值结果：低于预定线的概率，以及定义这条线的拒绝域。

branches.en: THE OLDER SENSE: importance, which statistics borrowed without replacing.
branches.cn: 较旧的义项：重要性，统计学借用了它却没有取代它。

branches.en: THE TEST AND ITS REPORT: a decision reduced to a number, and a convention that marks it with stars.
branches.cn: 检验与报告：被压缩成一个数的决定，以及用星号标记它的惯例。

branches.en: THE SIZE AND THE MULTIPLICITY: detectability separated from importance, and false alarms multiplied by many tests.
branches.cn: 大小与多重性：可检出性与重要性分开，误报被多次检验放大。

branches.en: THE MISREADING: a threshold result treated as proof of truth or magnitude.
branches.cn: 误读：把达到阈值的结果当作真实或效应大小的证明。

senses.title: The false-rejection threshold
senses.titleCN: 控制假阳性的概率阈值
senses.definition: the probability of rejecting a true null hypothesis that the researcher is prepared to accept
senses.definitionCN: 研究者愿意接受的、错误拒绝真零假设的概率
senses.example: The significance level fixes how much false alarm the test will tolerate.
senses.exampleCN: 显著性水平规定了检验愿意容忍多少误报。
senses.why: Before the data arrive, someone must decide how often a false alarm is acceptable, and that decision is the level.
senses.whyCN: 在数据到来之前，必须先决定多高的误报率可以接受，这个决定就是显著性水平。

senses.title: A conventional level such as five per cent
senses.titleCN: 百分之五这类惯用水平
senses.definition: one of the customary thresholds, such as five per cent or one per cent, used by a research community
senses.definitionCN: 研究共同体惯用的阈值，如百分之五或百分之一
senses.example: Most journals still expect a significance level of five per cent unless a stricter one is justified.
senses.exampleCN: 多数期刊仍期待百分之五的显著性水平，除非有理由采用更严格的标准。
senses.why: A convention saves every study from renegotiating the same number, even though the number itself is arbitrary.
senses.whyCN: 惯例免去每项研究重新谈判同一个数字，尽管这个数字本身是任意的。

senses.title: The rate of Type I error
senses.definition: the long-run proportion of true null hypotheses that will be rejected when the level is applied repeatedly
senses.definitionCN: 反复应用该水平时，真零假设被错误拒绝的长期比例
senses.example: Lowering the significance level reduces the Type I error rate but raises the chance of missing a real effect.
senses.exampleCN: 降低显著性水平会减少第一类错误率，却提高漏掉真实效应的机会。
senses.why: The level controls one side of the error trade-off, and the other side moves whenever this side is tightened.
senses.whyCN: 水平控制误差权衡的一端，这一端一收紧，另一端就移动。

senses.title: The critical value that matches the level
senses.definition: the boundary on the test statistic beyond which the result is declared significant
senses.definitionCN: 检验统计量超过即被判定为显著的边界
senses.example: Changing the significance level moves the critical value along the curve.
senses.exampleCN: 改变显著性水平会使临界值沿着曲线移动。
senses.why: A probability cannot be compared with the data directly, so the level is translated into a boundary on a statistic.
senses.whyCN: 概率无法直接与数据比较，因此水平被翻译成统计量上的边界。

senses.title: Adjustment for many comparisons
senses.definition: a stricter level used when many tests are run, so that the overall false-positive rate stays near the intended value
senses.definitionCN: 进行许多检验时采用的更严格水平，使总体假阳性率接近预定值
senses.example: The team lowered the significance level after running twelve subgroup tests.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在做了十二次子组检验之后降低了显著性水平。
senses.why: Each extra test spends part of the same error budget, so the level must be divided or the budget is overspent.
senses.whyCN: 每多一次检验就花掉同一笔误差预算的一部分，因此水平必须分割，否则预算超支。

senses.title: The link to confidence level
senses.titleCN: 与置信水平的对应关系
senses.definition: the complement of the confidence level, so that a five per cent significance level corresponds to ninety-five per cent confidence
senses.definitionCN: 置信水平的补数，例如百分之五的显著性水平对应百分之九十五的置信水平
senses.example: A significance level of five per cent matches a confidence level of ninety-five per cent.
senses.exampleCN: 百分之五的显著性水平对应百分之九十五的置信水平。
senses.why: The two numbers describe the same excluded tail from opposite directions, one as error and one as confidence.
senses.whyCN: 两个数字从相反方向描述同一条被排除的尾巴，一个叫误差，一个叫置信。

senses.title: The choice made before seeing data
senses.definition: the requirement that the level be fixed in advance and reported, so that it cannot be chosen to fit the result
senses.definitionCN: 要求在事前固定并报告水平，使其不能被挑选来迎合结果
senses.example: Pre-registration records the significance level before the analysis begins.
senses.exampleCN: 预注册在分析开始前就记录了显著性水平。
senses.why: Freedom to choose the level after seeing the data converts a test into a description of the analyst's preference.
senses.whyCN: 在看到数据后自由选择水平，会把检验变成对分析者偏好的描述。

senses.title: Its effect on power and decisions
senses.titleCN: 对检验功效与决定的影响
senses.definition: the trade-off in which a stricter level lowers false positives but also lowers the ability to detect real effects
senses.definitionCN: 更严格的水平降低假阳性，同时降低检出真实效应的能力所形成的权衡
senses.example: A very strict significance level can hide a real effect in a small study.
senses.exampleCN: 非常严格的显著性水平可能在小研究中掩盖真实效应。
senses.why: A threshold that admits almost nothing as significant also refuses many true findings, and that cost is called lost power.
senses.whyCN: 一个几乎不接受任何显著结果的阈值，也会拒绝许多真实发现，这个代价叫功效损失。

intro.en: Significance level joins significance, from Latin significantia, meaning or importance, to level, from Old French livel, a beam or balance.
intro.cn: 这个术语把来自拉丁语 significantia「意义、重要性」的 significance，与来自古法语 livel「横梁、天平」的 level 组合起来。

items.en: Significare meant to make a sign or convey meaning, from signum a sign and facere to make.
items.cn: significare 意为作出记号或传达意义，由 signum「记号」与 facere「做」构成。

items.en: Significantia named meaning or importance, and English took it as significance.
items.cn: significantia 指意义或重要性，英语借入为 significance。

items.en: Livel meant a beam or a balance, and the instrument for checking horizontality gave the word its later sense.
items.cn: livel 指横梁或天平，用来检查水平与否的器具赋予这个词后来的义项。

items.en: English used level for a flat surface and then for a position on a scale; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语用 level 指平面，后来指刻度上的位置；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Statistics borrowed level for the fixed probability of a test, so the phrase means a position on an error scale.
items.cn: 统计学借 level 表示检验的固定概率，因此这个短语指误差刻度上的一个位置。

items.en: The five per cent convention spread through twentieth-century practice, and its exact origin is debated.
items.cn: 百分之五的惯例在二十世纪实践中传播开来，其确切起源仍有争议。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like significance level; the second group names neighbouring quantities in a test.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 significance level 相近；第二组是与「检验量」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: Importance, or a probability below a threshold.
entries.definitionCN: 指重要性，或低于阈值的概率。

entries.definition: Important, or statistically beyond the threshold.
entries.definitionCN: 指重要的，或统计上超过阈值的。

entries.definition: To mean or indicate.
entries.definitionCN: 指意味着或标示。

entries.definition: A position on a scale, or a flat surface.
entries.definitionCN: 指刻度上的位置，或平面。

entries.definition: Too small to matter, or not beyond the threshold.
entries.definitionCN: 指小到不重要，或未超过阈值。

entries.definition: The boundary on a statistic that corresponds to the chosen level.
entries.definitionCN: 指与所选水平对应的统计量边界。

entries.definition: The proportion of true nulls mistakenly rejected.
entries.definitionCN: 指真零假设被错误拒绝的比例。

entries.definition: The chance of detecting a real effect when one exists.
entries.definitionCN: 指真实效应存在时检出它的机会。

entries.definition: The complement of the significance level, expressed as confidence.
entries.definitionCN: 指显著性水平的补数，以置信方式表达。

entries.definition: A boundary at which a decision changes.
entries.definitionCN: 指决定发生改变的边界。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations work through the real parts, word family and common phrases behind this term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想依托这个术语背后真实的构词部件、同族词与常见搭配。

normal.en: Significance carries meaning, and a level is a position on a scale, so the phrase names a position on an error scale.
normal.cn: 「显著性」带着「意义」，「水平」是刻度上的位置，这个短语指误差刻度上的一个位置。

normal.en: Five per cent is the conventional level, and it corresponds to ninety-five per cent confidence.
normal.cn: 百分之五是惯用水平，对应百分之九十五的置信水平。

normal.en: A stricter level means fewer false alarms and more missed effects.
normal.cn: 更严格的水平意味着更少误报、更多漏检。

normal.en: Multiple testing divides the same error budget among many tests.
normal.cn: 多重检验把同一笔误差预算分给许多次检验。

normal.en: The level is fixed before the data are opened, or it is not a test but a choice after the fact.
normal.cn: 水平在打开数据之前固定，否则就不是检验，而是事后挑选。

abstract.en: The level is a fence built before the race, and moving it after the race turns a measurement into a preference.
abstract.cn: 水平是赛前修好的栅栏，赛后移动它就把测量变成偏好。

abstract.en: A stricter gate keeps out false alarms and also keeps out some true guests.
abstract.cn: 更严的门把误报挡在外面，也把一些真的客人挡在外面。

abstract.en: The number five per cent is a social agreement more than a law of nature.
abstract.cn: 百分之五这个数字更像社会约定，而不是自然定律。

examples.en: The significance level must be reported with every test result.
examples.cn: 每项检验结果都必须报告显著性水平。

examples.en: They chose a significance level of one per cent because the decision was costly.
examples.cn: 由于决策代价高，他们选择了百分之一的显著性水平。

examples.en: The significance level was adjusted for the number of comparisons.
examples.cn: 显著性水平按比较次数作了调整。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「显著」加「水平」——先划一条线，决定能容忍多少误报，再看结果过不过线：显著性水平。

root: 拉丁 signum「记号」+ facere「做」→ significare「传达意义」→ significantia「意义、重要性」→ significance；古法语 livel「横梁、天平」→ 英语 level；统计学把 level 用作误差刻度上的位置，与 significance 组合成术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the threshold itself to its consequences: the false-rejection rate, conventional levels, Type I error, the critical value, multiple-testing adjustment, the link to confidence, pre-registration, and the effect on power.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从阈值本身走向后果：错误拒绝率、惯用水平、第一类错误、临界值、多重检验调整、与置信的联系、预注册，以及对功效的影响。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a distribution curve on a blackboard with a red vertical line, the area to its left painted red, and a note stating the acceptable false-alarm rate.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑板上一条分布曲线，一条红竖线立在偏左处，左侧面积被涂红，旁注可接受的误报比例。

branches.en: THE ERROR BUDGET: the acceptable rate of rejecting a true null, and the Type I error it controls.
branches.cn: 误差预算：可接受的错误拒绝真零假设的比例，以及它所控制的第一类错误。

branches.en: THE CONVENTION AND THE COMMITMENT: customary five per cent, and the duty to fix it before seeing data.
branches.cn: 惯例与承诺：惯用的百分之五，以及看数据前固定的义务。

branches.en: THE TRANSLATED BOUNDARY: the critical value that carries the level into the statistic.
branches.cn: 翻译后的边界：把水平带进统计量的临界值。

branches.en: THE SHARED AND MIRRORED NUMBER: adjustment for many tests, and the complement seen as confidence.
branches.cn: 共享与镜像的数字：多重检验的调整，以及作为置信的补数。

branches.en: THE PRICE: a stricter level buys fewer false alarms with lost power.
branches.cn: 代价：更严的水平换来更少误报，却损失功效。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin-derived noun for meaning to a French-derived noun for a balance beam.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁来源的「意义」名词与法语来源的「天平横梁」名词组合起来。

latinIntro.en: Latin signum and significare supply significance; Old French livel supplies level; the statistical sense of level is modern.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 signum 与 significare 提供「显著性」，古法语 livel 提供「水平」，「水平」的统计义是近代形成的。

definition_en: a range of values calculated from sample data that is expected to contain the true parameter at a stated confidence level over repeated sampling
core_image: 一条横轴，中间一个点估计，左右各伸出一段，被一只括号围住，括号两端标着刻度

senses.title: A range built around an estimate
senses.titleCN: 围绕估计值构造的范围
senses.definition: an interval computed from sample data so that it is likely to contain the unknown parameter
senses.definitionCN: 由样本数据算出、很可能包含未知参数的区间
senses.example: A confidence interval shows the range that repeated samples would usually bracket.
senses.exampleCN: 置信区间显示反复抽样通常会框住的数值范围。
senses.why: A single number hides its own uncertainty, so the interval gives the uncertainty a visible width.
senses.whyCN: 单个数字把自己的不确定性藏了起来，区间则给这份不确定性一个可见的宽度。

senses.title: The long-run coverage interpretation
senses.definition: the interpretation that, across many repeated samples, the stated proportion of such intervals will contain the true value
senses.definitionCN: 在大量重复抽样中，所述比例的区间会包含真值的解释
senses.example: A ninety-five per cent confidence interval does not mean a ninety-five per cent chance for this one interval.
senses.exampleCN: 百分之九十五的置信区间并不意味着这一个区间有百分之九十五的概率包含真值。
senses.why: The confidence belongs to the procedure that builds intervals, not to any single interval after it is built.
senses.whyCN: 信心属于构造区间的程序，而不属于建成之后的某一个区间。

senses.title: The confidence level
senses.definition: the stated proportion, usually ninety-five or ninety-nine per cent, attached to the procedure
senses.definitionCN: 附在程序上的所述比例，通常为百分之九十五或九十九
senses.example: Raising the confidence level widens the interval for the same data.
senses.exampleCN: 在数据相同的情况下，提高置信水平会使区间变宽。
senses.why: More confidence requires a wider net, and a wider net catches more but says less about where the value lies.
senses.whyCN: 更高的信心需要更宽的网，网更宽能兜住更多，却更难说清值在哪里。

senses.title: The margin around the point estimate
senses.definition: the distance from the estimate to each end of the interval, often built from a standard error and a multiplier
senses.definitionCN: 从估计值到区间两端的距离，常由标准误与倍数构成
senses.example: The confidence interval is the estimate plus and minus its margin.
senses.exampleCN: 置信区间就是估计值加减这段幅度。
senses.why: The interval is a point with two arms, and the arms carry the uncertainty the point cannot carry alone.
senses.whyCN: 区间是一个带两条臂的点，两条臂承载着点无法独自承载的不确定性。

senses.title: An interval for a difference
senses.definition: a range for the difference between two groups, used to judge whether the difference could plausibly be zero
senses.definitionCN: 两组差值所在的区间，用来判断差值是否可能为零
senses.example: The confidence interval for the difference included zero, so the effect was not established.
senses.exampleCN: 差值的置信区间包含零，因此效应尚未确立。
senses.why: A difference is itself an estimate, and its interval shows which directions and sizes remain plausible.
senses.whyCN: 差值本身也是一个估计，它的区间显示哪些方向与大小仍然可能。

senses.title: Interval versus credible interval
senses.titleCN: 置信区间与可信区间的区别
senses.definition: the contrast between a frequentist coverage interval and a Bayesian interval that carries a posterior probability
senses.definitionCN: 频率学派的覆盖率区间与带有后验概率的贝叶斯区间之间的对照
senses.example: A Bayesian credible interval answers a question that a confidence interval does not.
senses.exampleCN: 贝叶斯可信区间回答了一个置信区间不回答的问题。
senses.why: The two intervals can look alike on the page, but their probabilities are attached to different objects.
senses.whyCN: 两种区间在纸面上可能相似，但它们的概率附着在不同对象上。

senses.title: Width as a measure of precision
senses.definition: the way a narrower interval indicates a more precise estimate, usually because of a larger sample or less variation
senses.definitionCN: 区间越窄表示估计越精确，通常因为样本更大或变异更小
senses.example: The confidence interval narrowed after the second wave of data collection.
senses.exampleCN: 第二轮数据收集之后，置信区间变窄了。
senses.why: Width is the visible form of precision, and precision is bought with information.
senses.whyCN: 宽度是精确度的可见形式，而精确度是用信息换来的。

senses.title: Reading overlap between intervals
senses.definition: the practice of comparing two intervals to judge the plausibility of a difference, with care about what overlap does and does not prove
senses.definitionCN: 比较两个区间以判断差值是否可能，并注意重叠能证明什么、不能证明什么
senses.example: Overlapping confidence intervals do not by themselves prove that there is no difference.
senses.exampleCN: 置信区间重叠本身并不证明没有差异。
senses.why: Two wide intervals may overlap while the difference between their centres remains real.
senses.whyCN: 两个宽区间可以重叠，而它们中心之间的差异仍然真实存在。

intro.en: Confidence interval joins confidence, from Latin confidere, to trust fully, to interval, from Latin intervallum, the space between ramparts.
intro.cn: 这个术语把来自拉丁语 confidere「完全信任」的 confidence，与来自拉丁语 intervallum「城墙之间的空地」的 interval 组合起来。

items.en: Confidere meant to trust completely, from con- fully and fidere to trust.
items.cn: confidere 意为完全信任，由 con-「完全」与 fidere「信任」构成。

items.en: Confidentia named assurance or boldness, and English took it as confidence.
items.cn: confidentia 指确信或胆量，英语借入为 confidence。

items.en: Vallum meant a rampart or wall, and intervallum named the ground between two walls.
items.cn: vallum 指城墙或壁垒，intervallum 指两道墙之间的空地。

items.en: The noun widened from a space between walls to any gap in time or space.
items.cn: 这个名词从「墙间空地」扩展到时间或空间中的任何间隔。

items.en: English used interval for a gap and later for a set of values between two limits; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语用 interval 指间隔，后来指两个界限之间的一组取值；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Twentieth-century statistics joined the two nouns for a procedure-based range, and the exact origin of the phrase is debated.
items.cn: 二十世纪统计学把这两个名词组合成一种基于程序的区间，这个短语的确切起源仍有争议。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like confidence interval; the second group names neighbouring quantities in estimation.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 confidence interval 相近；第二组是与「估计量」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: Trust or assurance in a procedure or person.
entries.definitionCN: 指对程序或人的信任与把握。

entries.definition: Feeling sure about something.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某事感到有把握。

entries.definition: To trust someone with private information.
entries.definitionCN: 指把私密信息托付给某人。

entries.definition: A gap, or a set of values between two limits.
entries.definitionCN: 指间隔，或两界限之间的一组取值。

entries.definition: To come between; it looks close but its root is venire, to come.
entries.definitionCN: 指介入其间；形近但词根是 venire「来」。

entries.definition: The standard deviation of an estimate across repeated samples.
entries.definitionCN: 指估计量在反复抽样中的标准差。

entries.definition: A Bayesian range carrying a posterior probability.
entries.definitionCN: 指带有后验概率的贝叶斯区间。

entries.definition: The half-width of a survey interval around an estimate.
entries.definitionCN: 指调查中估计值两侧区间的半宽。

entries.definition: A single value used to estimate a parameter.
entries.definitionCN: 指用来估计参数的单个值。

entries.definition: The difference between the largest and smallest observed values.
entries.definitionCN: 指观测值中最大值与最小值之差。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations work through the real parts, word family and common phrases behind this term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想依托这个术语背后真实的构词部件、同族词与常见搭配。

normal.en: Confidence is trust, and interval is the ground between two walls, so the phrase names a trusted space between two limits.
normal.cn: 「信心」是信任，「区间」是两墙之间的空地，这个短语指两条界限之间一块受信任的空间。

normal.en: Ninety-five per cent confidence means the procedure covers the truth in ninety-five per cent of repeated samples.
normal.cn: 百分之九十五置信意味着这套程序在反复抽样中百分之九十五的情况下盖住真值。

normal.en: A wider interval is more confident and less precise at the same time.
normal.cn: 更宽的区间同时更自信也更不精确。

normal.en: An interval that includes zero leaves the possibility of no difference open.
normal.cn: 包含零的区间使「没有差异」这一可能保持开放。

normal.en: A credible interval and a confidence interval can share a shape but not a meaning.
normal.cn: 可信区间与置信区间可以形状相同，含义却不同。

abstract.en: An interval is a net thrown around an unknown fish, and confidence describes the net, not the fish.
abstract.cn: 区间是撒向未知之鱼的一张网，信心描述的是网，而不是鱼。

abstract.en: The single number is a dot; the interval is the shadow the dot casts when uncertainty is the light.
abstract.cn: 单个数字是一个点，区间是当不确定性成为光源时那个点投下的影子。

abstract.en: Two intervals may overlap like two conversations in a corridor, without either speaker agreeing.
abstract.cn: 两个区间可以像走廊里的两段对话那样重叠，而两位说话者并未达成一致。

examples.en: The paper reports a confidence interval for every estimated coefficient.
examples.cn: 论文为每个估计系数报告了置信区间。

examples.en: A confidence interval that includes zero suggests the effect may be absent.
examples.cn: 包含零的置信区间提示效应可能不存在。

examples.en: The confidence interval was wide because the sample was small.
examples.cn: 由于样本小，置信区间很宽。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「置信」加「区间」——一个点不够，给它左右各伸一条臂，圈出一个可能范围：置信区间。

root: 拉丁 confidere「完全信任」← con-「完全」+ fidere「信任」→ confidentia → 英语 confidence；拉丁 vallum「城墙」→ intervallum「墙间空地」→ 英语 interval；二十世纪统计学把两者组合为置信区间。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from construction to reading: the range around an estimate, long-run coverage, the confidence level, the margin, intervals for differences, the contrast with credible intervals, width as precision, and the reading of overlap.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从构造走向解读：围绕估计值的区间、长期覆盖率、置信水平、两侧幅度、差值区间、与可信区间的区别、宽度即精确度，以及区间重叠的解读。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a horizontal axis with a point in the middle, arms extending both ways, and a bracket closing around the arms.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条横轴，中间一个点，左右各伸出一条臂，一只括号把两条臂围住。

branches.en: THE BUILT RANGE: an estimate with two arms, each arm carrying uncertainty.
branches.cn: 构造的范围：一个带两条臂的估计，每条臂承载不确定性。

branches.en: THE PROCEDURE'S PROMISE: long-run coverage, and the confidence level that states it.
branches.cn: 程序的承诺：长期覆盖率，以及陈述它的置信水平。

branches.en: THE DIFFERENCE: an interval that can include zero and leave no effect established.
branches.cn: 差值：一个可以包含零、使效应无法确立的区间。

branches.en: THE ALTERNATIVE AND THE PRECISION: a Bayesian interval beside it, and width as visible precision.
branches.cn: 替代与精确：旁边的贝叶斯区间，以及作为可见精确度的宽度。

branches.en: THE COMPARISON: overlap read with care about what it does not prove.
branches.cn: 比较：谨慎解读重叠不能证明什么。

senses.title: The half-width around a survey estimate
senses.definition: the distance on either side of an estimate within which the true value is expected to lie at a stated confidence
senses.definitionCN: 在给定置信度下真值预计落在估计值两侧的距离
senses.example: The margin of error shrinks as the sample grows larger.
senses.exampleCN: 样本越大，误差范围越小。
senses.why: A survey cannot report a point without also reporting how far the point may be from the truth.
senses.whyCN: 调查不能只报一个点而不报这个点可能离真相多远。

senses.title: A quantity computed from standard error
senses.definition: a multiple of the standard error, fixed by the chosen confidence level and the sampling design
senses.definitionCN: 标准误的倍数，由所选置信水平与抽样设计决定
senses.example: The margin of error is usually about twice the standard error for a ninety-five per cent interval.
senses.exampleCN: 对于百分之九十五的区间，误差范围通常是标准误的两倍左右。
senses.why: The formula turns uncertainty into a single distance that a reader can compare with the estimate.
senses.whyCN: 公式把不确定性变成一个读者可以与估计值比较的距离。

senses.title: Its relation to sample size
senses.definition: the shrinkage of the margin as the square root of the sample size grows
senses.definitionCN: 误差范围随样本量的平方根增大而缩小
senses.example: Doubling the sample reduces the margin of error by only about one third.
senses.exampleCN: 样本量翻倍只能把误差范围缩小约三分之一。
senses.why: Information reduces uncertainty slowly, and the square root is the price of every extra decimal of precision.
senses.whyCN: 信息降低不确定性的速度很慢，平方根就是每多一位精确度要付的代价。

senses.title: Sampling error versus other error
senses.definition: the part of the total error that comes from sampling, as distinct from non-response, wording or coverage problems
senses.definitionCN: 总误差中来自抽样的部分，区别于无应答、措辞或覆盖问题
senses.example: The reported margin of error covers sampling error but not the bias of a self-selected panel.
senses.exampleCN: 所报告的误差范围涵盖抽样误差，却不涵盖自选样本组的偏差。
senses.why: A formula can measure the error it was built for, and it cannot measure the errors outside its model.
senses.whyCN: 公式只能测量它为之所以被造出来的那种误差，测不了模型之外的误差。

senses.title: Tolerance in measurement
senses.definition: the permitted deviation of an instrument reading or manufactured part from its stated value
senses.definitionCN: 仪器读数或制造零件相对标称值所允许的偏差
senses.example: The margin of error for the gauge was stated as one millimetre.
senses.exampleCN: 该量具的误差范围标为一毫米。
senses.why: The same phrase serves engineering and statistics because both need a band around a stated value.
senses.whyCN: 同一个短语同时服务工程与统计，因为两者都需要在标称值周围给出一个容许带。

senses.title: The plus-or-minus convention
senses.definition: the common reporting form in which an estimate is followed by plus or minus the margin
senses.definitionCN: 常见报告形式：估计值后面跟上正负误差范围
senses.example: The poll reported forty-two per cent plus or minus the margin of error.
senses.exampleCN: 民调报告为百分之四十二，加减误差范围。
senses.why: The convention compresses a range into a sign, and the sign travels more easily than the method behind it.
senses.whyCN: 惯例把一个区间压缩成一个符号，而符号比背后的方法更容易传播。

senses.title: Its political misuse
senses.definition: the treatment of a statistical band as a verdict about a lead, a win or a loss
senses.definitionCN: 把统计上的容许带当作关于领先、胜选或落败的裁决
senses.example: A lead inside the margin of error is often reported as a tie.
senses.exampleCN: 处于误差范围之内的领先常被报道为平手。
senses.why: A band that describes uncertainty is read as a threshold of victory, which is a change of meaning rather than a calculation.
senses.whyCN: 描述不确定性的容许带被读成胜负门槛，这是意义的改变，而不是计算。

senses.title: Its difference from the confidence level
senses.definition: the distinction between the width of the band and the probability attached to the procedure that produced it
senses.definitionCN: 容许带的宽度与产生它的程序所附概率之间的区别
senses.example: A higher confidence level enlarges the margin of error without making the estimate more accurate.
senses.exampleCN: 提高置信水平会扩大误差范围，却不会使估计更准确。
senses.why: The level says how often the band works, and the margin says how wide the band is.
senses.whyCN: 水平说这条带多久有效，误差范围说这条带有多宽。

intro.en: Margin of error joins margin, from Latin margo, an edge, to error, from Latin errare, to wander or stray.
intro.cn: 这个短语把来自拉丁语 margo「边缘」的 margin，与来自拉丁语 errare「游走、迷失」的 error 组合起来。

items.en: Margo meant an edge or a border, and English kept the spatial sense in margin.
items.cn: margo 意为边缘或边界，英语在 margin 中保留了空间义。

items.en: Margin named a blank edge and later an amount of room allowed; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: margin 指空白边，后来指被允许的余量；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Errare meant to wander or stray from a path, not yet to be wrong in an argument.
items.cn: errare 意为游走或偏离道路，当时还不指论证出错。

items.en: Error named a wandering or a straying, and English extended it to any departure from truth.
items.cn: error 指游走或偏离，英语把它扩展到任何对真相的偏离。

items.en: English used error for mistakes of many kinds, including measurement; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语用 error 指多种错误，包括测量错误；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Survey statistics joined the two nouns for the allowed band around an estimate, and the phrase became standard in polling.
items.cn: 调查统计学把这两个名词组合成估计值周围的容许带，这个短语在民调中成为标准说法。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like margin of error; the second group names neighbouring quantities in survey estimation.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 margin of error 相近；第二组是与「调查估计量」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: An edge, a blank border, or an allowed amount.
entries.definitionCN: 指边缘、空白边或允许的余量。

entries.definition: A departure from truth or from a correct value.
entries.definitionCN: 指对真相或正确值的偏离。

entries.definition: To make a mistake.
entries.definitionCN: 指犯错。

entries.definition: Based on error; incorrect.
entries.definitionCN: 指基于错误的；不正确的。

entries.definition: The standard deviation of an estimate across samples.
entries.definitionCN: 指估计量在样本间的标准差。

entries.definition: The full range around an estimate, of which the margin is half the width.
entries.definitionCN: 指估计值周围的完整区间，误差范围是其半宽。

entries.definition: Error caused by studying a sample rather than the whole population.
entries.definitionCN: 指因研究样本而非总体造成的误差。

entries.definition: Error from response, wording, coverage or processing rather than from sampling.
entries.definitionCN: 指来自应答、措辞、覆盖或处理而非抽样的误差。

entries.definition: The permitted deviation of a part or reading.
entries.definitionCN: 指零件或读数被允许的偏差。

entries.definition: A measure of spread among observations.
entries.definitionCN: 指观测值离散程度的度量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations work through the real parts, word family and common phrases behind this term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想依托这个术语背后真实的构词部件、同族词与常见搭配。

normal.en: Margin is an edge, and error is a wandering, so the phrase names the edge of a wandering estimate.
normal.cn: 「边距」是边缘，「误差」是游走，这个短语指一个游走估计的边缘。

normal.en: The margin is half the confidence interval, not the whole interval.
normal.cn: 误差范围是置信区间的一半，而不是整个区间。

normal.en: Quadrupling the sample halves the margin of error.
normal.cn: 样本量变为四倍，误差范围减半。

normal.en: A reported margin usually covers sampling error only.
normal.cn: 所报告的误差范围通常只涵盖抽样误差。

normal.en: A lead inside the margin is not a safe lead.
normal.cn: 处在误差范围之内的领先不是稳妥的领先。

abstract.en: The estimate is a boat, the margin is its wake, and the wake shows how far the boat may drift.
abstract.cn: 估计是一条船，误差范围是它的尾迹，尾迹显示船可能漂多远。

abstract.en: Precision is purchased with sample size at a square-root exchange rate.
abstract.cn: 精确度用样本量购买，汇率是平方根。

abstract.en: A band that means uncertainty can be read as a band that means victory, and the reading changes the politics.
abstract.cn: 一条表示不确定性的带可以被读成表示胜利的带，而读法改变了政治。

examples.en: The poll's margin of error was three percentage points.
examples.cn: 这次民调的误差范围是三个百分点。

examples.en: Any difference smaller than the margin of error should be treated as inconclusive.
examples.cn: 任何小于误差范围的差异都应当视为尚无定论。

examples.en: The margin of error does not cover the bias of a volunteer sample.
examples.cn: 误差范围并不涵盖自愿样本的偏差。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「边缘」加「错误」——数字旁边留一条边，表示它可能偏离多少：误差范围。

root: 拉丁 margo「边缘」→ 法语 marge → 英语 margin；拉丁 errare「游走、偏离」→ 法语 errour → 英语 error；调查统计学把两者组合为估计值周围的容许带 margin of error。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the survey band to its misuse: half-width, formula, sample-size relation, sampling versus other error, instrument tolerance, the plus-or-minus convention, political misuse, and the difference from the confidence level.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从调查容许带走向误用：半宽、公式、与样本量的关系、抽样与其他误差、仪器容许差、正负号惯例、政治误用，以及与置信水平的区别。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a printed survey result with a plus-or-minus bracket drawn beside the number, and an editor circling the bracket in red.
core.cn: 核心意象：一页印出的调查结果，数字旁画着正负括号，编辑用红笔把括号圈出。

branches.en: THE BAND AND THE FORMULA: half the interval, computed from the standard error.
branches.cn: 容许带与公式：区间的一半，由标准误算出。

branches.en: THE PRICE OF PRECISION: sample size reduces the band only by its square root.
branches.cn: 精确的代价：样本量只能按平方根缩小容许带。

branches.en: THE COVERED AND UNCOVERED ERROR: sampling error inside the formula, bias outside it.
branches.cn: 被覆盖与未被覆盖的误差：公式内的抽样误差，公式外的偏差。

branches.en: THE ENGINEERING AND PRINTED FORMS: tolerance on a gauge, and plus or minus in a report.
branches.cn: 工程与印刷形式：量具上的容许差，报告里的正负号。

branches.en: THE MISREADING AND THE DISTINCTION: a band read as a verdict, and width confused with confidence.
branches.cn: 误读与区分：容许带被读成裁决，宽度与信心被混淆。

senses.title: The general process of examining data

senses.whyCN: 原始记录本身不回答问题，必须先被整理才能说话。

senses.title: Statistical analysis
senses.definition: the use of summary measures, models and tests to describe data and judge hypotheses
senses.definitionCN: 用汇总指标、模型与检验来描述数据并判断假设
senses.example: The statistical part of data analysis estimated the effect and its interval.
senses.exampleCN: 数据分析中的统计部分估计了效应及其区间。
senses.why: When the question is about size and uncertainty, the analysis needs a probability model.
senses.whyCN: 当问题涉及大小与不确定性时，分析就需要一个概率模型。

senses.title: Analysis of qualitative material
senses.definition: the systematic reading and coding of interviews, documents or observations to identify themes and meanings
senses.definitionCN: 对访谈、文件或观察进行系统阅读与编码，以识别主题与意义
senses.example: Data analysis of the transcripts produced four themes and a revised coding frame.
senses.exampleCN: 对逐字稿的数据分析产生了四个主题与一版修订编码框架。
senses.why: Not all evidence arrives as numbers, and text needs its own disciplined route from raw record to finding.
senses.whyCN: 并非所有证据都以数字到来，文本需要自己那条从原始记录到发现的严谨路径。

senses.title: Cleaning and preparation
senses.definition: the work of detecting missing values, errors, duplicates and inconsistencies before modelling begins
senses.definitionCN: 在建模开始前发现缺失值、错误、重复与不一致的工作
senses.example: Most of the data analysis time went into cleaning the merged files.
senses.exampleCN: 大部分数据分析时间花在清洗合并后的文件上。
senses.why: Every model assumes the table is already coherent, and someone must make that assumption true.
senses.whyCN: 每个模型都假定表格已经自洽，而必须有人把这个假定变成事实。

senses.title: Exploratory analysis
senses.definition: an open-ended examination of patterns, distributions and anomalies before a formal hypothesis is fixed
senses.definitionCN: 在正式假设确定之前，对模式、分布与异常进行的开放式考察
senses.example: Exploratory data analysis revealed a cluster that the original design had not expected.
senses.exampleCN: 探索性数据分析揭示出原始设计没有预料到的一个群体。
senses.why: The analyst first looks around the data without a verdict in mind, so that surprise can still occur.
senses.whyCN: 分析者先不带结论地环视数据，这样惊讶才有可能发生。

senses.title: Confirmatory analysis
senses.definition: a planned test of a stated hypothesis using rules fixed before the data are examined
senses.definitionCN: 用查看数据之前固定的规则，对已陈述假设进行计划性检验
senses.example: Confirmatory data analysis requires the model to be specified in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 验证性数据分析要求模型预先写明。
senses.why: Once a hypothesis is fixed, the analysis becomes a fair test rather than a search for a story.
senses.whyCN: 假设一旦固定，分析就成为公平检验，而不是寻找故事。

senses.title: Computational analysis
senses.definition: the use of algorithms, databases and software to process data at a scale beyond hand calculation
senses.definitionCN: 用算法、数据库与软件处理超出人工计算规模的数据
senses.example: The data analysis pipeline ran overnight on the cluster.
senses.exampleCN: 这条数据分析流水线在集群上跑了一整夜。
senses.why: Scale changes the method: what is possible with a thousand rows is not the same as what is possible with a billion.
senses.whyCN: 规模改变方法：一千行的可能与十亿行的可能不是一回事。

senses.title: Interpretation and reporting
senses.definition: the step that turns results into statements about the world, with limits, assumptions and uncertainty made explicit
senses.definitionCN: 把结果转化为关于世界的陈述，并明确限度、假设与不确定性
senses.example: The final stage of data analysis is writing what the numbers do and do not support.
senses.exampleCN: 数据分析的最后一步，是写清这些数字支持什么、不支持什么。
senses.why: A table of results is not yet a finding; someone must state what it means and where it stops.
senses.whyCN: 一张结果表还不是发现，必须有人说明它意味着什么、到哪里为止。

intro.en: Data analysis joins data, the plural of Latin datum, something given, to analysis, from Greek analusis, a loosening or dissolving.
intro.cn: 这个术语把 data（拉丁语 datum「被给予之物」的复数）与 analysis（希腊语 analusis「拆解」）组合起来。

items.en: Dare meant to give, and the participle datum named a thing given or granted.
items.cn: dare 意为给予，分词 datum 指被给予或授予之物。

items.en: Datum named a given fact, and its plural data became the English mass noun for records.
items.cn: datum 指给定的事实，其复数 data 成为英语中指记录的物质名词。

items.en: English used data for facts and later for digital records; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语用 data 指事实，后来指数字记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Analusis meant a loosening or resolving of a compound into its parts.
items.cn: analusis 意为把复合体拆解为各部分的松开过程。

items.en: Ana- meant up or throughout, and luein meant to loosen; together they describe taking something apart.
items.cn: ana- 意为向上或贯穿，luein 意为松开；合起来指把某物拆开。

items.en: Statistics and computing joined the two words for the whole workflow from records to conclusions; the phrase is twentieth-century.
items.cn: 统计学与计算把这两个词组合成从记录到结论的完整流程；这个短语属二十世纪。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like data analysis; the second group names neighbouring stages of working with evidence.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 data analysis 相近；第二组是与「处理证据」意思相邻的阶段。

entries.definition: Records, measurements or facts in any form.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何形式的记录、测量或事实。

entries.definition: A single given fact or measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个给定的事实或测量值。

entries.definition: The breaking of a whole into its parts for examination.
entries.definitionCN: 指把整体拆成部分加以考察。

entries.definition: To carry out such an examination.
entries.definitionCN: 指进行这样的考察。

entries.definition: A person who performs analysis.
entries.definitionCN: 指从事分析的人。

entries.definition: The science and practice of summarising and testing data.
entries.definitionCN: 指对数据进行汇总与检验的学问与实践。

entries.definition: Detecting and correcting errors before analysis.
entries.definitionCN: 指在分析前发现并纠正错误。

entries.definition: Searching large datasets for unsuspected patterns.
entries.definitionCN: 指在大数据集中搜寻未预料到的模式。

entries.definition: Assigning meaning to results.
entries.definitionCN: 指为结果赋予意义。

entries.definition: Labelling qualitative material into categories.
entries.definitionCN: 指把定性材料标注为各类别。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations work through the real parts, word family and common phrases behind this term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想依托这个术语背后真实的构词部件、同族词与常见搭配。

normal.en: Data is the plural of a word for something given, and analysis is a loosening, so the phrase means loosening what was given.
normal.cn: 「数据」是「被给予之物」的复数，「分析」是「松开」，这个短语指把被给予的东西拆开。

normal.en: Cleaning comes before modelling, because a model cannot repair an inconsistent table.
normal.cn: 清洗在建模之前，因为模型无法修复一张自相矛盾的表格。

normal.en: Exploratory analysis looks around, while confirmatory analysis tests a promise made earlier.
normal.cn: 探索性分析四处环视，验证性分析检验早先作出的承诺。

normal.en: The last step is not a number but a sentence with limits attached.
normal.cn: 最后一步不是一个数字，而是一句带着限度的话。

normal.en: Computing changed the scale of data analysis without changing its need for a question.
normal.cn: 计算改变了数据分析的规模，却没有改变它对问题的需要。

abstract.en: Data do not speak; analysis is the grammar that makes them audible.
abstract.cn: 数据不会说话，分析是使它们可被听见的语法。

abstract.en: A clean table is already an argument about what counts as an error.
abstract.cn: 一张干净的表格本身已经是关于「什么算错误」的论证。

abstract.en: The model at the end inherits every decision made at the beginning.
abstract.cn: 最后的模型继承了开始时的每一个决定。

examples.en: The paper describes the data analysis in enough detail for replication.
examples.cn: 论文对数据分析的描述详细到可以复做。

examples.en: Data analysis was separated from data collection to reduce the risk of bias.
examples.cn: 数据分析与数据收集分开，以降低偏差风险。

examples.en: The data analysis showed a pattern that the original hypothesis had not predicted.
examples.cn: 数据分析显示出一个原假设没有预测到的模式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「数据」加「分析」——先把杂乱表格洗干净，再拆开看结构，最后写成一句可核查的话：数据分析。

root: 拉丁 dare「给予」→ 过去分词 datum「被给予之物」→ 复数 data；希腊 analusis「拆解」← ana-「贯穿」+ luein「松开」→ 英语 analysis；统计学与计算把两者组合为 data analysis。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move through the workflow: the general process, statistical analysis, qualitative analysis, cleaning, exploration, confirmation, computation, and interpretation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着流程展开：总体过程、统计分析、定性分析、清洗、探索、验证、计算，以及解释。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of raw tables on a desk, a screen with a cleaned chart beside them, and deleted error rows in the wastebasket.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上一叠原始表格，旁边屏幕显示清洗后的图表，废纸篓里装着删掉的错误行。

branches.en: THE WORKFLOW AND THE CLEANING: the whole sequence, and the unglamorous work that makes it possible.
branches.cn: 流程与清洗：完整顺序，以及使顺序成为可能的琐碎工作。

branches.en: THE TWO KINDS OF EVIDENCE: numbers handled statistically, and texts handled qualitatively.
branches.cn: 两类证据：用统计处理的数字，用定性处理的文本。

branches.en: THE TWO MODES OF INQUIRY: looking around before a hypothesis, and testing one fixed in advance.
branches.cn: 两种探究方式：假设前的环视，与预先固定假设后的检验。

branches.en: THE SCALE: algorithms and software processing more than hands can hold.
branches.cn: 规模：算法与软件处理超出人手所能掌握的数据。

branches.en: THE SENTENCE AT THE END: results converted into a claim with limits.
branches.cn: 结尾的句子：结果被转换成带限度的话。

intro.en: The phrase joins the plural of a Latin participle meaning given to a Greek noun meaning a loosening.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语「被给予」的分词复数与希腊语「拆解」名词组合起来。

latinIntro.en: Latin dare and datum supply data; Greek ana- and luein supply analysis; English plurals and compound syntax do the joining.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dare 与 datum 提供「数据」，希腊语 ana- 与 luein 提供「分析」，英语复数形式与复合句法完成连接。

items.example: It supplies the participle behind data.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 data 背后的分词。

items.example: The singular still names one measurement.
items.exampleCN: 单数仍指一个测量值。

items.example: English treats it as a mass noun.
items.exampleCN: 英语把它当作物质名词。

items.example: It marks taking a whole apart.
items.exampleCN: 它标出把整体拆开。

items.example: It supplies the dissolving image in analysis.
items.exampleCN: 它提供 analysis 中「拆解」的意象。

items.structure: Greek noun from ana- plus luein
items.example: It becomes English analysis.
items.exampleCN: 它成为英语 analysis。

items.meaning: the separation of a whole into parts
items.example: The second half names the operation.
items.exampleCN: 后半命名这一操作。

items.example: It forms analyse; American spelling uses -ize.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 analyse；美式拼写作 -ize。

items.example: It forms analyst.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 analyst。

items.meaning: the workflow from records to claims
items.example: The compound is modern and covers many methods.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是现代用语，涵盖多种方法。

latinEntries.structure: analysis, analysis (f., third declension, from Greek analusis)

definition_en: the analysis of non-numerical material such as interviews, documents or observations in order to identify themes, meanings and patterns
core_image: 长桌上铺开三份访谈稿，彩色便签把相似句子连成几组，墙上贴着一张主题网络图

sceneCN: 这里指对非数值材料的系统分析（第 1 个义项：非数值材料的分析）；句意为定性分析寻找的是意义与模式，而不是系数。图中可辨识物件：访谈稿、彩色便签、主题网络图、长桌、记号笔。
